method.scope: All Hebrew occurrences of אין כאן מקום להאריך and variants, שמעתי and קבלתי throughout the five Dover Tzedek source parts. Screenshots of names/vitality and purifying the sheretz included.
method.searchOrder: For oral traditions: Mei HaShiloach, then the 2492 original Beit Yaakov footnotes and other Ishbitz–Radzin works, then Rav Tzadok expansions. For elaboration cues: Rav Tzadok developments and precise Ishbitz–Radzin parallels.
method.attribution: New passages are labeled Parallel; a matching idea does not by itself establish the unnamed oral teacher. Circular anthology reprints of Dover were excluded as independent evidence.
method.display: One note per selected source, number at the Hebrew cue; bold exact source reference with a complete fresh English translation of the selected Hebrew excerpt.
method.fidelity: All selected Hebrew excerpts checked in original raw source files; omissions marked by ellipses. Existing 2570 notes preserved exactly.
method.variation: When the point is already explained, a different Rav Tzadok work is used to add depth. Identical repeated quotations were replaced with verified alternatives.
method.latestZip: rav-tzadok-library (5).zip compared: primary texts unchanged; all7404DoverHebrew phrases identical; updated cited caches only differ in formatting.

trigger.he: ועצם התחלתה באל״ף: "אנכי", שהוא מצד מה שכלה חד, התחלתה באל״ף, ואין כאן מקום להאריך

results.reason: A substantial elaboration from a different work than the already quoted Ohr Zarua LaTzadik: the aleph of Anochi expresses the primordial root in which Israel’s final perfection is already present, although it is revealed only later. This extends the existing note rather than repeating its account of unity and combination.
results.hebrewQuote: ופתיחת התורה בא' דאנכי דמשם נובע שורש התורה מעומק ראשית של הדבור, ומשם זכו לשני הכתרים נגד נעשה ונשמע היינו נגד תורה ועבודה שהוא כתר תורה וכתר כהונה דעדיין לא זכה אהרן ונטלו, ונקראו אז כל ישראל ממלכת כהנים, ובמתן תורה היה ההשגה בהתגלות ובגאולת מצרים היה דבר זה בהעלם עדיין רק השם יתברך הודיע זה למשה העתיד להיות דבהוציאך וגו' תעבדון וגו', וזהו הוראת מלת אהיה לשון עתיד דרצה לומר שאני עתיד להיות עמהם, וזהו בריש כל דרגין דעדיין לא הגיע לסוף ושלימות הכנסת ישראל הוא בסוף כל דרגין, ובראשית המחשבה היה זה התכלית והסוף כבר מגולה דבשביל זה התחיל כל סדר השתלשלות המדרגות,
results.translation: Torah opens with the aleph of “Anochi,” for from there the root of Torah flows from the profound beginning of speech. From there they merited the two crowns corresponding to “We will do” and “We will hear”—that is, corresponding to Torah and divine service: the crown of Torah and the crown of priesthood, for Aaron had not yet merited and received it. All Israel were then called “a kingdom of priests.” At the giving of the Torah this apprehension was revealed; at the redemption from Egypt this matter was still hidden. Only the blessed God informed Moses of what would occur in the future: “When you bring out … you shall serve … .” This is the meaning of the word Ehyeh in the future tense: “I shall be with them.” This belongs to the head of all levels, where the end has not yet been reached, whereas the perfection of the Congregation of Israel is at the end of all levels. At the beginning of thought, this purpose and end were already revealed, for the entire sequence of descending levels began for its sake.
results.heading: Further elaboration: Machshavot Charutz 8:17

trigger.he: ויש בזה דברים ארכים בענין שבירת לוחות הראשונות, ואין כאן מקום להאריך

results.reason: Direct expansion by Rav Tzadok on the breaking of the first tablets, the second tablets, and the relation between Written and Oral Torah.
results.hebrewQuote: וזה סוד שבירת הלוחות ראשונות שהיו מן השמים ונתקיימו על ידי האחרונות שהיו על ידי משרע"ה כמו שאמרו ז"ל על פסוק פסל לך, והאחרונות עצמן חזרו להיות ראשונות ובמקום לוחות ראשונות אחר תיקון החטא, וקודמין להם דלוחות ושברי לוחות מונחים בארון (ברכות ח' ע"ב), והלוחות קודמין שהן עיקר
results.translation: This is the mystery of the breaking of the first tablets, which came from Heaven, and their establishment through the latter tablets, which came through Moshe Rabbeinu, as our Sages said concerning “Carve for yourself.” After the sin was repaired, the latter tablets themselves again became the first tablets and took the place of the original tablets. They take precedence over the broken ones, for the tablets and the fragments of the tablets lie in the Ark (Berachos 8b), and the tablets come first because they are the essential ones.
results.heading: The First and Second Tablets: Revelation and Human Participation

trigger.he: כמו שכתוב: "ובא השמש וטהר", ושמעתי פרוש "וכשיבוא השמש" על דרך: "כי שמש ומגן השם אלהים"

results.reason: Independent Ishbitz parallel explains the exact sun-and-shield verse and the unrestricted divine light. It is not asserted to identify the source of Rav Tzadok’s heard gloss. The anthology and original Beit note2052 merely repeat Dover Tzedek and were excluded as circular.
results.hebrewQuote: זה שאמר הכתוב (תהילים פ״ד:י״ב) כי שמש ומגן ה' אלהים חן וכבוד יתן ה' לא ימנע טוב להולכים בתמים, איתא בזוה"ק פקודי (רכד:) שמש דא הוא רזא דשמא קדישא יקו"ק דהכא קיימין כל דרגין לנייחא, ומגן דא איהו רזא דשמא קדישא דאקרי אלהים. ורזא דא דכתיב (לך טו) אנכי מגן לך. ושמש ומגן דא איהו רזא דשמא שלים. חן וכבוד יתן ה' למהוי כלא רזא חדא. שמש הוא שם הוי"ה הנקרא שמש, ומצד זה השם לא היה יכול להתהוות שום התהוות בריאה בעולם, כי הכל היה נכלל באורו הגדול יתברך. כי כשיתראה אור זה בעולם יתראה שאין מציאות בעולם רק השי"ת לבדו
results.translation: This is what Scripture says in Psalms (84:12): “For Hashem God is a sun and a shield; Hashem grants grace and glory; He withholds no good from those who walk uprightly.” The holy Zohar, Pekudei (224b), teaches: “The sun is the mystery of the holy Name Havayah, where all the levels rest; the shield is the mystery of the holy Name called Elokim. This is the mystery of ‘I am a shield for you’ (Lech Lecha, Genesis 15:1). Sun and shield are the mystery of the complete Name. ‘Hashem grants grace and glory’—so that everything should be the mystery of one unity.” The sun is the Name Havayah, which is called sun. From the standpoint of this Name, no created existence could come into being in the world, because everything would be included in His great light. For, when this light is revealed in the world, it will be seen that nothing exists in the world but Hashem alone.
results.heading: Parallel in Beit Yaakov: The Divine Sun and Its Shield

results.hebrewQuote: ויקחו לי תרומה. הוא ע"פ מה שפרשנו בפסוק (משלי ט"ו, כ"ד) אורח חיים למעלה למשכיל [לעיל פ' וירא ד"ה וירא א']. היינו שזה העיקר והראשית בכל דבר ליתן על לבו שאורח חיים למעלה, היינו הש"י שהוא נותן חיים ורכוש לכל אדם הוא למעלה כמו דבר המונח למעלה, וזה ג"כ ויקחו לי תרומה היינו שישראל יקחו אותו ית' מרומם וראשית בכל דבר, וזה דאיתא בגמ' דסנהדרין [ק"ב:] מהיכן בעי למשרי המוציא מהיכן דקדים בישולו, הענין הוא כמו דאיתא במס' ברכות [ל"ה.] כתיב לה' הארץ ומלואה וכו', וכתיב והארץ נתן לבני אדם, כאן קודם ברכה כאן לאחר ברכה, כי ענין ברכה מורה שמכיר שיש לו אדון ומאתו בא לו ההשפעה, ואם אתה מכיר זאת אז תוכל לומר ברוך אתה לנוכח הש"י, וע"ז נאמר והארץ נתן לבני אדם. וזה ג"כ השאלה מהיכן בעי למשרי המוציא, היינו היכן הוא ההכרה בזה הככר שהש"י הוא הנותן ותוכל לומר עליו ברוך אתה, מהיכן דקדים בישולו, היינו כי כל מעשה הככר, האדם עושה בידיו הלישה והעריכה והיסק התנור ונותן כל הככר בשוה אל התנור וזה המקום שקדם להתבשל זה אינו מכח האדם, ומתחיל ליתן אל לבו, מפני מה זה המקום דווקא קדים להתבשל אין זה רק רצון הש"י, ע"כ שייך מזה המקום דווקא לברך המוציא.
results.translation: “They shall take a contribution for Me.” This follows what we explained concerning “The path of life is above for the understanding person” (Proverbs 15:24; above, Parashas Vayera, the first passage beginning “Vayera”): the essential first step in everything is to take to heart that the path of life is above—that Hashem, who gives life and possessions to every person, is above, like something placed above. So too “They shall take a contribution for Me” means that Israel should regard Him as exalted and first in everything. This is the meaning of the Gemara’s question in Sanhedrin (102b): From which part should one begin cutting the bread for the blessing Hamotzi? From the part that baked first. The explanation accords with Berachos (35a): it is written, “The earth and its fullness belong to Hashem,” and it is written, “He gave the earth to human beings”; one refers to before a blessing, the other to after a blessing. A blessing expresses recognition that one has a Master and that one’s bounty comes from Him. If you recognize this, you can address Hashem directly and say, “Blessed are You”; concerning this it says, “He gave the earth to human beings.” This is also the question, From where should one begin Hamotzi? Where in this loaf is the recognition that Hashem is the giver, so that one can say “Blessed are You” over it? From the part that baked first. For a person makes the whole loaf with his hands—kneading, shaping, heating the oven—and puts the entire loaf into the oven equally. But the fact that this particular part baked first is not due to human power. He begins to consider: Why did this particular part bake first? It is nothing but Hashem’s will. Therefore it is specifically from this part that one should recite the blessing Hamotzi.
results.heading: Parallel in Mei HaShiloach: Recognizing the Giver Before Receiving His Gift

A blessing expresses recognition that one has a Master and that one’s bounty comes from Him. If you recognize this, you can address Hashem directly and say, “Blessed are You”; concerning this it says, “He gave the earth to human beings.” This is also the question, From where should one begin Hamotzi? Where in this loaf is the recognition that Hashem is the giver, so that one can say “Blessed are You” over it? From the part that baked first. For a person makes the whole loaf with his hands—kneading, shaping, heating the oven—and puts the entire loaf into the oven equally. But the fact that this particular part baked first is not due to human power. He begins to consider: Why did this particular part bake first? It is nothing but Hashem’s will. Therefore it is specifically from this part that one should recite the blessing Hamotzi.
results.heading: Parallel in Mei HaShiloach: Recognizing the Giver Before Receiving His Gift

results.translation: “My son, if you receive my words and treasure my commandments with you, inclining your ear to wisdom…if you seek it like silver and like hidden treasures…then you will understand…and find knowledge of God.” At first, “inclining your ear to wisdom” is stated as a command, whereas afterward it says “if you seek it.” For inclining the ear to wisdom and directing the heart to understanding lie within human power. results.translation: This is the meaning of the two loaves of Shavuos, which come as chametz: it is the offering to Hashem of the leaven in the dough that obstructs us, as stated in Berachos (17a). Through this one merits receiving the giving of the Torah, which is the seasoning for the inclination (Kiddushin 30b)—using it only in accordance with Hashem’s will. Then it is “very good,” as our Sages expounded in Bereishis Rabbah, and as stated in Berachos (34a) concerning leaven: a little is beneficial, but much is harmful. This is the “little folly” that is more precious than wisdom and honor. Wisdom is the apprehension of words of Torah themselves; honor is what follows from it at the end, for “the wise shall inherit honor.” The little folly brings a person to all this through his feeling of deficiency: through it he longs, desires, and hopes for words of Torah, so that through them he may complete what he lacks.
results.heading: The Leaven in the Dough: Desire Redirected Toward Torah

results.translation: From the human side, the principal effort is through awe, as explained. This is also [the order] in the verse, “Turn away from evil and do good.” From Hashem's side, however, “I am” comes first, as the root of the positive commandments, and afterward “You shall have no other gods,” as the root of the prohibitions. Likewise, the Arizal arranged the Shabbos meals: the Friday-night meal corresponds to the holiness of our father Yitzchak, peace be upon him, and the morning meal to our father Avraham, peace be upon him. As explained, from the human side effort is through awe, and afterward one merits love from Hashem. But the Holy One created the souls of the patriarchs—as it says, “I took Avraham,” and so forth—and Avraham was born first, and Yitzchak afterward. Likewise, in Nisan they merited illumination from Hashem for a time, and afterward it immediately disappeared. At the splitting of the Sea, a maidservant saw [what Yechezkel did not see], and so forth; nevertheless, afterward they sought to gaze, as indicated by “the wilderness of Shur,” and as stated in the holy Zohar. Only the desire remained within them. Concerning this it says, “I remember for you the kindness of your youth,” and so forth, “your following Me into the wilderness.” Through that desire, they placed “We will do” before “We will hear.” Nevertheless, the evil inclination still remained and could entice them. For this comes the month of Iyar: to purify us from our husks, to repair everything through repentance. This prepares for the month of Sivan, the giving of the Torah, when the Angel of Death—which is the evil inclination, as Bava Basra 16a says—was annulled, as it says, “I said: You are divine beings,” as stated in Avodah Zarah 5a.

results.translation: “They shall send from the camp every person afflicted with tzaraas, every zav, and everyone defiled by a corpse.” The person afflicted with tzaraas represents anger, for tzaraas comes for the sin of evil speech (Arachin 15b). The zav is a person of desire, while one defiled by a corpse represents sadness. Therefore the person afflicted with tzaraas is sent outside all three camps, because the attribute of anger has no portion in Israel. The zav is sent only outside the camp of the Levites and the camp of the Shechinah, meaning that the attribute of desire does not befit Torah scholars. One defiled by a corpse is sent only outside the camp of the Shechinah, for even among Torah scholars the attribute of sadness is sometimes found, as stated in the Gemara (Taanis 4a): “The Torah is what inflames him”; this heated agitation is sadness. He is sent only from the camp of the Shechinah, for “strength and joy are in His place.”
results.heading: Parallel in Mei HaShiloach: Desire and the Three Camps

results.translation: This is why the month of Nisan is the new year for kings. It would have been fitting for it to be on the first of Sivan, when the Torah was given to Israel, concerning which it is written, “Through Me kings reign.” But first it says “Through Me, kings,” and afterward “they reign”: one must first be king over oneself. This occurs in Nisan, when Israel restrict themselves to eating the bread of poverty, accept the Creator’s yoke, and eat from His hand a dry piece of bread without taste, rather than delicacies beneath the yoke of flesh and blood. For in Egypt they truly possessed abundant good, as it says in Exodus (16:3), “When we sat….” Through this “they reign,” meaning over the whole world; this occurs in Sivan through the Torah that was given in it.

results.translation: It is known that the last level of any order is the head of the levels that follow it. One who is a tail to lions is a head to foxes, as stated in Sanhedrin (37a). Moreover, the last level encompasses all the levels that transmit their influence to the recipient. It therefore contains all the levels together from the standpoint of giving forth their influence; this is the meaning of the circles. The first level, by contrast, is the beginning of receiving the influence—that is, the root of all the levels from the standpoint of what they receive from above. This is the meaning of the surrounding light, as explained.

results.translation: But Raaya Mehemna, in this portion, page 230a, enumerates all ten sefiros alluded to in the name Havayah: Yud-Heh are Wisdom and Understanding, Vav is the six attributes, and the final Heh is Kingship, as written in the holy Zohar, in this portion, page 258a. The upper tip of the Yud alludes to Nothingness, as written in Zohar III, 65b. Here it says that the ten sefiros are also alluded to in the name Adnus. It enumerates “kind” and “mighty,” and likewise “He is truth and she is faith”; “She is prophet and she is prophecy” [as printed] corresponds to Hod. Opposite the attribute Netzach, the level of Moshe, it enumerates “He is humble and she is humility”; “He is righteous and she is righteous [in the feminine]”; “He is king and she is kingship.” Afterward it enumerates the first three sefiros: “He is wise and she is wisdom,” etc. It says: “Because of this the Rabbis established: anyone whose interior is not like his exterior,” etc.—for He is the interior and His Shechinah the exterior; He is within and she is outside. But in the Gemara, concerning a person, the meaning is reversed: his exterior looks good, and his interior must also be good like his exterior. Here in the holy Zohar the meaning is that even the exterior, the name Adnus, is like the interior, the name Havayah, as it says: “That which is outside does not differ from that which is inside,” etc. “Because Havayah is concealed within, He is called only through His Shechinah, Adnus.” This is because in truth everything is one, and in the World to Come the pronunciation too will be through Havayah.
results.heading: Parallel: Peri Tzadik, Pinchas 17:1

results.translation: The holiness of Shabbos is fixed and established from the Blessed Name, who sanctified it during the days of Creation, as written in Pesachim (117b). results.translation: The Torah likewise states explicitly concerning a priest entering the service, “They shall wash their hands and feet,” etc. So too with Shabbos, which is in time what the Sanctuary is in place, as explained many times: when entering Shabbos, one must wash oneself. The Sages likewise instituted washing the hands for a meal, supporting it with “Sanctify yourselves”—these are the first waters (Berachos 53b, at the end). The washing indicates that one does not intend one’s own enjoyment; this is holiness. On Shabbos, all Israel’s eating is in holiness. Shammai the Elder’s practice was to eat all his days in honor of Shabbos (Beitzah 16a), wishing every day’s meal to be a mitzvah-meal through intending it in honor of Shabbos. Hillel had a different practice: he said that he could intend for the sake of Heaven even in weekday eating, as though feeding a guest, as stated concerning Hillel in Vayikra Rabbah 34. He knew nothing at all of his own enjoyment, as explained at the end of Toldot, discourse 2. This is the meaning of washing the hands, which is a mitzvah, over which we bless, “Who has sanctified us through His commandments.” It resembles the washing of hands over the heifer whose neck is broken: one has no personal interest in this and does not intend bodily enjoyment. This is “Sanctify yourselves.” On Shabbos, when one attains the additional soul—the crowns mentioned above—this means that one repairs the serpent’s corruption. Consequently, all Israel’s eating is in holiness.
results.heading: Purifying the Hands before Entering Holiness

Through these garments Adam merited to feel the light of Shabbos even though it had not yet been given to him. The fourth, “and brightness around it,” is the shell of nogah, the root of all kinds of permitted desires, which do have rectification. From the root of those three shells the three worlds—Creation, Formation, and Action—were damaged, for they contain a mixture of evil: these are the ofanim, chayos, and seraphim. In the human soul they are nefesh, ruach, and neshamah, which can be damaged through prohibitions by the root of these three shells, whereas chayah and yechidah are encompassing light and are not damaged. Now, if a person has damaged and corrupted all three of his aspects—his mind, heart, and instruments of action, which are the aspects of nefesh, ruach, and neshamah—in all seven holy attributes in each, “refined sevenfold,” meaning forty-nine gates in each, nevertheless he still has hope to be purified through repentance from the depths of the heart, which is the fiftieth gate present in each. This is what our Sages hinted at concerning Rabbi Meir’s student, who could purify the creeping creature: it alludes to the three impure shells as a whole. Even if a person, Heaven forbid, became impure through them all, he can nevertheless be purified through the fiftieth gate present in each. This is the meaning of “one hundred and fifty reasons”: the three fiftieth gates, through which there is hope to be purified from all three shells. With this allusion King Shlomo made the sea, which held one hundred and fifty purifying mikvaos, for in his days rectification of all defects had already reached its complete perfection; then the moon stood in its fullness, resembling the future. But sin caused the setback, so we still needed further clarifications until the time of the end.
results.heading: Peri Tzadik, Vaetchanan 3:2 — the deeper meaning of “purifying the sheretz”

results.translation: The meaning of their disagreement is that we find three occasions concerning the eradication of Amalek. In the generation of Moses, Amalek confronted them and they fought against him, etc.: “Joshua weakened Amalek”—he merely weakened his power. In the generation of Mordecai and Esther, Haman likewise provoked them and sought “to destroy, to kill, and to annihilate”; afterward, “it was reversed, so that the Jews themselves ruled over those who hated them.” This differs from the generation of Samuel, when we do not find at all that Amalek provoked Israel; rather, God commanded Samuel and Saul to place everything belonging to Amalek under the ban. The explanation is that, in the wilderness, when the time had come for the revelation of the Written Torah, Amalek provoked Israel to prevent them from receiving the Written Torah. This occurred at Rephidim, named for their having slackened their hold on words of Torah (as stated in Sanhedrin 106a). This came about through Amalek, who cast upon them a slackening of their hands in words of Torah, because he knew that through the giving of the Torah he would be entirely nullified. As stated in Shemot Rabbah 41, there would be freedom from the angel of death. This would occur through the nullification of the evil inclination that caused the damage: it is the angel of death; it is the evil inclination (as stated in Bava Batra 16a). And Amalek is the evil inclination, as stated in the holy Zohar (III, 160a).

results.translation: “Sarah denied, saying: I did not laugh.” The depth of the matter is that what is stated in the Gemara (Berachos 33b), “Everything is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven,” is only according to the limits of human intellectual perception. In truth, everything is in the hands of Heaven, even the fear of Heaven; only in this world has the Blessed Name concealed His way. The attribute of our father Yitzchak was to recognize that even the fear of Heaven is in the hand of the Blessed Name, but the world was not worthy of so precious a thing. Therefore Sarah had to say, “My master is old,” appearing to deny that everything is in the hands of Heaven. Through this the Holy One, blessed be He, showed her measure for measure that even the fear of Heaven is in His hand; this was the birth of Yitzchak. Without this concealment, which was hidden from her, our father Yitzchak could not have been born in this world, for the preciousness of his attribute was to clarify and show that even the fear of Heaven is in the hands of Heaven, and even all Israel’s sins are within the providence of the Blessed Name, for through this His great Name will be magnified and sanctified. Understand, for it is very, very deep.
results.heading: Parallel: Mei HaShiloach I, Vayera 3 — “everything is in the hands of Heaven”

results.translation: The judgments of Hashem that pass over a person do not reach the depth of his root, for the Blessed Name created a time for everything to return to its holding. He created the Jubilee year so that then every person would return to the place and holding belonging to him from Hashem, as it is said, “The Jubilee year shall be holy to you.” This means that in the Jubilee year the light of the holiness of the Blessed Name will be revealed to everyone’s eyes through sounding the shofar on Yom Kippur, until it is recognized that whatever holding he has from his ancestors through the gift of the Blessed Name will remain his. What came into his hand through human action, even though it was his acquisition until now and was in his possession, must nevertheless be returned to its proper place, because it is not his at the root. This is the illumination of the Blessed Name in the Jubilee year: everyone can recognize the place belonging to each thing. They come to this recognition and understanding after fulfilling the mitzvah of Shemittah—surrendering everything to the Blessed Name. Through this they reach the attribute “What is Yours is Yours”: they recognize where everything belongs at the root. As the Midrash says, “All are presumed blind until the Holy One, blessed be He, illuminates their eyes.” Although to human eyes the servant appears to belong to his master, and the field to the one who bought it, one for whom the Holy One illuminates and opens his eyes sees that all human deeds cannot change the depth of the will of the Blessed Name even by a hair’s breadth. In the Jubilee this light will be revealed.

results.translation: Likewise, the statement “Who is a person of the World to Come? One who joins redemption to the evening prayer” does not mean merely joining the words in spoken recitation. Rather, the matter of the redemption from Egypt, which we were commanded to remember constantly every day, is to remember the illumination of light from the Blessed Name that took place at the Exodus. Through all the plagues they left the shell and entered the ten holy attributes. At the ninth plague it is written, “For all the children of Israel there was light,” and afterward, in the tenth plague, the light was greater; at the splitting of the sea a maidservant saw what Yechezkel did not see. In mentioning redemption one must mention the plague of the firstborn and the splitting of the sea, as written in the Yerushalmi and Shemos Rabbah, chapter 22. Remembering means that the light of the first day should shine in the heart. This is the mitzvah of remembering the Exodus every day, and joining this to prayer, which is like standing before a king, the attribute of kingship. One says, “Adnus, open my lips”; the name Adnus opens the mouth, so that the Shechinah speaks from his throat, as written in Noam Elimelech concerning “From where do we know that the Holy One, blessed be He, prays?”—meaning, through the mouths of the children of Israel. “His prayer is fluent” is an expression of being sent as an emissary.

results.translation: In every generation there are two leaders, corresponding to Mashiach ben David and Mashiach ben Yosef, particularly in the footsteps of the Messiah. They correspond to the two levels of penitents and the wholly righteous, and in every generation they open these two gates anew. Every Jewish soul contains both, for both encompass the entire nation: all Israel are called after Yosef, “the remnant of Yosef,” and after Yehudah, “Jews.” This is their principal name, because “there is no righteous person on earth”; from Yosef they are only a remnant, for the main part was assimilated and lost in the exile of the Ten Tribes. That is, everyone has matters in which he is righteous, as the early authorities explained at the beginning of the chapter Kol HaYad concerning donkey drivers: regarding one matter they are called fit, and regarding another wicked. In those matters he is at the level of a wholly righteous person. … For Yosef the righteous one’s level is to follow a straight line without deviation. In this, each person follows his own line, and there is no mingling of portions. By contrast, when someone sinned and became bent, and then returns to make the crooked straight, his boundary expands by the measure of the line’s bend. Every bent line extends farther toward the side to which it bends; when one wishes to make it straight, one must thicken the line by the width of the bend, and it becomes a thick, broad, straight line. This is the penitents’ advantage over the wholly righteous: through this, their boundary expands farther.
results.heading: The Two Messiahs and the Two Paths within Every Soul

results.translation: A thousand is from the side of the Blessed Name, as stated in the Gemara: the blessing of the Holy One, blessed be He, is a thousand. Ten is human perception, and a hundred represents the clarifications of this world. Therefore we say three times, “Holy, holy, holy,” to show the connection between human perception and His blessed light. The first “Holy” is ten, corresponding to human perception; the second “Holy” is a hundred, indicating all the clarifications of this world; and the third “Holy” is a thousand, from the side of the Blessed Name. This alludes to the connection between human perception and the Blessed Name through one’s action, service, and clarifications in this world. The name Yud-Heh Vav-Heh also indicates this: Yud-Heh alludes to the higher world, which is from the Blessed Name alone. Corresponding to this, King David said the fifteen Songs of Ascents to raise the deep. The lower Vav-Heh indicate the lordship of the Creator, which is in this world amid very great concealment, and the Vav indicates human action: through human action and service there is a connection from the lower world to the higher world.

results.translation: The unification and interweaving of the two Names is what is stated in Tanna Devei Eliyahu Rabbah, chapter 3: “I feared from within my joy, and rejoiced from within my fear.” In truth, the essence of the Blessed Name is one, singular and unique; there are only two lights, meaning two kinds of apprehension for the perceiving human soul. When it apprehends the indwelling of the Blessed Name within it, it reaches fear and shame before Him; when it apprehends the unlimited light, it reaches joy. The purpose of all service and performance of the mitzvos is the unification of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah: to attain more apprehension of the Blessed Name through understanding of heart and mind. This means that the light of the Shechinah increases within him—the light and apprehension of Divinity dwelling within him—by becoming united for him with the unlimited light. He contemplates that He is truly one, singular and unique: the light dwelling within him, which he apprehends and which is indicated by Adnus, is united with the name Havayah; all is one. It is itself the unlimited light, before which nothing among all the world’s creatures interposes now, just as before the world was created.

results.translation: “Eleven days from Chorev.” When they received the Torah, Israel’s heart had not yet been refined so as to follow Hashem’s will completely. They understood intellectually that it was good for them to fulfill His will, but their heart was not refined. Upon entering the Land, their heart was refined. This is what Moshe told them: “Eleven days from Chorev.” When you were at Chorev and received the Torah, you thought your heart was already refined, because you had traveled in three days. In truth it was not so: there was a distance of eleven days, and you had not acquired words of Torah so that they would become fixed in your heart. Only after the forty years, through stumbling and trials, was your heart refined, for one does not stand upon words of Torah unless one has stumbled over them (Gittin 43a). Concerning this David said, “In vain do you rise early … eat the bread of sorrows; so He gives His beloved sleep.” Before a person’s heart has been refined, he needs effort and sorrow before fulfilling Hashem’s will. But once words of Torah have become fixed in his heart, the Holy One grants him Torah even without effort, even during sleep, and he need not exert himself so greatly.
results.heading: Parallel in Mei HaShiloach: before and after forty years

results.translation: In truth they said in Avos, “Study is not the principal thing, but action,” and in Kiddushin (40b), “Study is greater because it leads to action.” In Shabbos (88a) they likened “we shall do” to the fruit and “we shall hear” to the leaves. In truth Torah scholars are the clusters of fruit and the unlearned are the leaves, as they said in Chullin (92a). Nevertheless even for Torah scholars, action is the principal thing, as they said in Yevamos (109b): whoever is not engaged in action is not engaged in learning; he does not even possess Torah. In Berachos (17a), “The purpose of wisdom…”—it does not say “those who learn them,” but “those who do them.” It also says that one must not read and study and then rebel. This includes refraining from a transgression and sitting without acting: one likewise receives reward as for performing a mitzvah when it comes before him and he escapes it, as in Kiddushin (39b). This is what Hashem asks of you: fear of Him. It is the beginning, and the purpose of wisdom is fear of Hashem, through which one is restrained from transgressions. As they said in the Yerushalmi, if you come to rebel, know that you are God-fearing, and one who fears does not rebel. Through turning from evil, doing good follows of itself, like one mitzvah drawing another, and caution against transgression leads to alacrity in a mitzvah.
results.heading: Rav Tzadok’s expansion: why study leads to action

results.translation: This is “Hashem has not given you a heart to know.” After they had passed through many concealments in the wilderness—as it says, “Who led you through the great and fearsome wilderness, with serpent, fiery serpent, and scorpion”—this indicates the concealments they experienced. results.translation: In this world the Holy One has nothing in His world but the treasury of fear of Heaven alone. Fear is the awakening from below, as is known: concerning it it says, “This is the gate,” for it is the gateway through which to enter faith. A person’s first entry into Hashem’s service is through fear of Heaven, which is the beginning of wisdom—that is, the beginning of recognizing that Hashem exists, for chacham in Aramaic means recognition. Immediately fear and submission reach him, as in Rema’s words at the beginning of Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chaim. It says, “What does Hashem ask … except to fear”: what is sought from a person is only the attribute of fear. Love, however, cannot be attained through a person’s effort, for love exists only between similar beings; how can the axe boast to its hewer that it loves him? Rather, Hashem in His abundant compassion and kindness calls the congregation of Israel “My sister” and “My perfect one”—My twin—and says, “I have loved you.” When Hashem loves a person, the person of himself loves Him as well.

Hashem acted for His sake and His praise, and saw that everything was very good and pleasing to Him. Then He ceased and rested on the seventh day, rejoicing and delighting in His works. The same occurs in the preceding thought. After a person has pictured everything through the wisdom in his mind, he then feels, through the understanding in his heart, the joy he will have when the matter is brought into actuality according to his desire and the conception formed by his wisdom. Through this joy and the longing within his heart, he afterward brings the action into complete realization. Thus the six days of activity receive from the preceding Shabbos within thought and heart, and bestow upon the actual Shabbos that follows them. This is the mystery of Binah and Malkhus, as is known, with the six extremities of Zeir Anpin between them.

results.translation: “The wisdom of women builds her house.” The wisdom of women is patience and a settled mind, that in every matter one should have restraint over one’s spirit. This is wisdom clothed in understanding, as the Zohar says (Acharei, 65a), “Because we call her Mother, female, might and judgment issue from her.” This is what the Gemara says in Sanhedrin (109b): the wife of On son of Peles saved him. It is this understanding within him, that he should be patient and settled in his affair—why should he go out to war? As the Gemara says in Yevamos (65b), a man’s way is to conquer, and it is not a woman’s way to conquer; she does not wish to enter the responsibility of danger. This is what the Gemara says in Niddah (45b), “He teaches that the Holy One gave a woman greater understanding than a man”; understanding is the restraining power, as in the Zohar (Bo, 42a). This is “builds her house”: a fixed possession in holiness. “But foolishness tears it down with her hands”: foolishness is wanting to grow proud, go out to battle, and overpower everything, without considering his ways, whether he has the power to prevail. As it says in Proverbs (14:3), “In the mouth of a fool is a rod of pride, but the lips of the wise guard them.” He is the opposite of the wise person, who guards his soul, mouth, and tongue.

Isaac’s attribute is might: after this became clarified and Hashem’s revelation descended into this world, this is called might, as the Gemara says, “Thus Moses heard from the mouth of Might” (Megillah 31b). Isaac was likewise called Hashem’s might in the world. “These are the generations of Isaac son of Abraham,” etc., means that Isaac our father’s offspring is the publicizing of Hashem’s revelation in this world. “Abraham begot Isaac” means that this came through Abraham’s yearning, for yearning is Abraham’s attribute. results.translation: Lishmah, by contrast, cannot be constant at all, for lishmah means cleaving. Its measure is like the conjugal period of Torah scholars, once a week: one cannot attain cleaving except on Shabbos; or, for those who stroll—the ones who stroll in the well-known Pardes—at most once a day. Constant activity, however, is not lishmah; rather, “from within,” etc., means that from within the not-lishmah itself, from its interior and inwardness, that very study comes to be lishmah. This happens through the fear that awakens him, regarding which it is said, “If fear of Hashem is his treasury, yes,” etc. This is “Happy is the person who fears always”: it refers to his constant occupation, for certainly at intervals he reaches the level of cleaving, at which no fear at all is necessary.
results.heading: Lishmah as Cleaving, Especially on Shabbos

results.translation: Even forbidden things contain a holy spark that gives them life, but it is imprisoned there in a house of bondage, unable to emerge. Therefore eating them is forbidden until the final time, when Hashem releases the bound. This will be at the Messiah’s coming, in the feast of the Leviathan, when the spirit of impurity is removed from the earth. Even in this world, it can sometimes be repaired through a mixture in which it becomes nullified and returns to a permitted state. This must happen without a person’s knowledge or intention to nullify it, for one does not nullify a prohibition in the first instance; rather, it must become mixed on its own. By human intention it is impossible to raise them and take them out of the house of bondage, the place where the king’s prisoners are bound, in the depths of the three impure shells.
results.heading: “Hashem Releases the Bound” and the Release of Forbidden Sparks

results.translation: “A man of kindness bestows kindness upon his soul.” This means bestowing kindness and doing what benefits one’s body, like Hillel’s statement upon entering the bathhouse: “Let us go and bestow kindness upon this poor creature” (Vayikra Rabbah 34:3). This is the attribute of piety. But all this applies after a person has refined himself so that he does not taste bitter as sweet. Then, if he withholds good from his body when it is within his power, it is said of him, “One who troubles his flesh is cruel” (Proverbs 11:17). If, however, he has not yet been clarified in this matter and desires to pamper his body, it says of him, “The wicked performs false actions.” Not only is this not called kindness to his body; on the contrary, he damages his body through the luxuries of his delicacies. These are false actions. This is what the holy Zohar, Shemos 200a, hints at with “three points for the Torah”: in every matter, small or great, a person should weigh in the balance whether the deed contains three things—benefit to his body, as the Sages said, “At first, when a person acts, he acts for himself” (Pesachim 68b); goodness and uprightness in Hashem’s paths; and the absence of any harm arising from it to others. Once he has made this reckoning, he may perform the deed, and it is called “bestowing kindness upon his soul,” etc.
results.heading: Parallel in Mei HaShiloach: Hillel’s care for his body as kindness

results.translation: This is the convert’s contention in the chapter BaMeh Madlikin and Shammai’s strictness in pushing him away. Shammai is the level of awe, as is known, from which come might and strictness—the level of Isaac our father, peace be upon him, from whom the name Israel begins, as explained above, section 1. Therefore he pushed away the converts there in BaMeh Madlikin; see there. From the standpoint of awe, perfection in it is precisely the opposite, as explained above. Hillel’s humility drew them near, like Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, who was exceedingly humble and therefore drew near the mixed multitude and argued concerning Micah, as explained above. Abraham our father was likewise humble, as stated in Berachos: “Woe for the humble one,” etc., a disciple of Abraham our father; therefore he is father to converts, as taught in Bikkurim. For from humility—assessing one’s deficiency against Hashem’s greatness—there is no place for exaltation over this convert who comes with his staff and bag. The One who said, etc., will say to vinegar that it should burn, and can place light within vinegar too, in the manner of “Create a pure heart for me, O God.” Creation is something from nothing, and this is not the place to elaborate on it.
results.heading: Shammai’s Awe and Hillel’s Humility

results.translation: “A rain of free gifts You wave, O God; Your inheritance, when it was weary, You established.” Rain hints at an outpouring of bounty. “Free gifts” means with goodwill, unlike one who gives unwillingly and afterward turns his face away from the recipient; rather, the outpouring will be filled with generosity and willingness. “You wave, O God” is an expression of comfort, like fanning someone who is distressed by heat. “Your inheritance, when it was weary”: Israel’s weariness, without renewed desire, arises because they are Your inheritance and therefore remain in simplicity. Therefore “You established it”: bestow words of Torah upon them to restore their soul.
results.heading: Divine Rain Renews Desire When Israel Grows Weary

results.translation: “Love your fellow as yourself; I am Hashem.” Through the commandment to love your fellow as yourself, Heaven’s honor grows. By nature, a person brings all the good he acquires into his own possession. Where does the desire come from to benefit his fellow, giving him some of what Hashem has granted him? From knowing that just as he was created by Hashem, his fellow was also created by Hashem: do we not all have one Father, did not one God create us? Why should we, the offspring blessed by Hashem, withhold kindness from one another? It also comes from knowing that his own might and the strength of his hand did not make his wealth; it is Hashem’s gift, and consequently he will fulfill the Giver’s will with it. Thus, through loving his fellow as himself, Heaven’s honor grows. One must also fulfill this commandment in the following way: just as a person loves himself even though he knows himself and his deficiencies, and his self-love nevertheless covers all his failings, so he must love his fellow even when he knows that his fellow has deficiencies. This is what “I am Hashem” teaches: just as Hashem loves both of you although He knows your deficiencies, as the Gemara teaches, “Either way you are called children,” etc. (Kiddushin 36a).
results.heading: Parallel in Mei HaShiloach: divine recognition and love of one’s fellow

results.translation: Afterward he thought: how can a person glorify himself in this? Therefore it says, “Abraham sojourned in the land of the Philistines for many days.” The Midrash, Metzora 19:5, says that days of distress are called many days. He therefore underwent the trial of the binding of Isaac, to begin clarifying himself and clarifying all the preceding trials. They all depended upon this trial, and he could, Heaven forbid, lose them all. Concerning this it says, “You have given those who fear You a banner to be raised, because of truth, forever” (Psalms 60:6). The Midrash, Vayera 55:1, expounds this verse concerning the trial of the binding, for in the binding it is said, “By Myself I have sworn, declares Hashem,” and Hashem’s Name endures forever. This means that this truth and its veracity will stand as a merit for all generations forever. Once he saw that he possessed the power to surrender everything to Hashem, he understood that in all he had undergone until then, he had performed Hashem’s will.
results.heading: Actual Trial Clarifies the Righteous Person’s Earlier Service

results.translation: The Zohar, Va’era, teaches that in Egypt speech was in exile. This means that they were good in their hearts, but not so when it came to actual expression in deed. This follows what I heard concerning “a fool of lips falters”: it means that he cannot bring something from potential into actuality, as the Sages said in Sotah on “a people that does not understand shall falter,” concerning the sotah waters’ inability to bring their action into effect. Speech is the explicit revelation of what is in the heart. For this they instituted joining redemption to prayer: one sometimes cries out to Hashem in one’s heart, yet cannot express it in speech with such purity, without any alien thought, and truly coming from the heart. This is Egypt’s redemption: their redemption is the redemption of this capacity. By mentioning it, this is effected within a person, enabling him to speak words of prayer with his whole heart.
results.heading: From an Inward Cry to Actual Words of Prayer

results.translation: In truth, the holy Zohar Chadash also states what Rambam says. The Ari likewise writes that in one place there is knowledge, and there is no choice there at all: this is in Atika. Concerning this the Gemara said in Shabbos 89b, “If your sins are like the years”—those ordered and coming from the six days of creation—“they shall become white as snow.” There is no place there for human action at all, for Hashem thus created the deeds of the wicked from the beginning: first darkness, then light. Choice was granted only within the attributes of the seven days of creation. As for understanding how knowledge does not conceal choice from a person, concerning this Scripture says, “My thoughts are not your thoughts, nor are your ways My ways,” as Rambam explains.
results.heading: Divine Knowledge and the Realm of Human Choice

results.translation: “The tribe of Joseph’s sons speaks rightly.” The matter is that this passage, which applies only for its particular time, was written at the Torah’s conclusion. Its purpose is to show Israel that “man does not live by bread alone, but by every utterance of Hashem’s mouth.” Bread means the general words of Torah needed by everyone, at every time and for every soul, without any change or substitution: the six hundred and thirteen commandments. The essential thing, however, is to understand through words of Torah, at every time, Hashem’s will—what He desires at every moment, according to the time and occasion. From words of Torah, light emerges into Israel’s hearts so that they understand the depth of Hashem’s will according to the time. This passage was therefore written after the entire Torah’s conclusion, to make Israel understand that particulars emerge from the whole Torah for every time and occasion. All words of Torah are counsels through which a person can understand what Hashem desires now and engage in it. Therefore this passage, which likewise applies only for a particular time, was written.
results.heading: Discerning Hashem’s Will in Each Particular Moment

results.translation: “The earth was tohu and bohu, with darkness over the face of the deep.” The Gemara, Chagigah 12a, teaches: tohu is a green line surrounding the entire world, from which darkness emerges; bohu consists of moist stones submerged in the deep, from which water emerges. The meaning is that tohu is the opposite of kindness, for kindness is the great expansion of the outpouring. Tohu is its opposite: fear. Creation feared to bestow upon the created world and entrust it to human hands, lest a person spoil it by receiving this world’s bounty and acting against Hashem’s will with it, forgetting that Hashem bestowed it upon him. Creation therefore contracts the outpouring, as it says, “He did not create it tohu; He formed it to be inhabited” (Isaiah 45:18).
results.heading: The Green Line as Creation’s Fear and Restraint

results.translation: “Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king,” etc., “and his mother’s name was Cheftzi-bah,” etc. The meaning of Manasseh is that he was born with exceedingly great awe, beyond a person’s power to bear such awe. In truth, awe is intensified in every king, as the Gemara teaches in Berachos 34b: once a king bows, he does not straighten again. Manasseh’s awe was greater still, and the entire sin he committed consisted in seeking ways to remove this awe from himself so that he would possess free choice, for the intensity of the awe had taken choice away from him. Heaven brought about his birth with such great awe, the opposite of King David, peace be upon him, whose attribute was love.
results.heading: A King’s Overwhelming Awe and Manasseh’s Attempt to Escape It

results.translation: The first waters mean washing the hands, which are the instruments of action, for action is everywhere attributed to the hands. They are to be clean of every stain and defilement of outward desire, solely for God, to sustain one’s body according to His will. This is accomplished by washing in water, the water of knowledge, which is Torah, as it says, “I created Torah as its seasoning.” The evil inclination is always the desire in the heart, as it is written, “the inclination of the heart,” and desire is everywhere attributed to the heart: “the heart desires.” Nevertheless, the Sages said, “If the Holy One did not help him,” and so forth: only the beginning comes from the person, as in “Open for Me,” and “I shall open.” This resembles Moshe’s request, “May it be Your will that the Divine Presence rest in your handiwork”: God helps bring the act to its complete perfection. This is “you shall be holy,” the last waters: after eating, he washes his hands so that they too are clean of the filth of this world. As the Sages expounded in Yoma: a person sanctifies himself, and they sanctify him from above. Therefore the first waters are a mitzvah: mitzvos are the human being’s special portion, through which he fulfills “sanctify yourselves,” and so he blesses, “Who has sanctified us through His commandments.” The last waters are an obligation: God sanctifies him as a debt from which there is no exemption. The oil alludes to wisdom, the clear knowledge and recognition that “I am your God.” This comes after proper eating, fittingly for God’s sake, to sustain one’s soul; wisdom and knowledge of God are then added to him.
results.heading: First waters and last waters: preparation and Divine completion

results.translation: According to what I have written, one may explain: from the statement that Gehinnom comes to an end, it follows necessarily that “shall not be extinguished” is not forever. He explains it as referring to the great Day of Judgment, when all the other wicked will already have received their judgment and their fire will have been extinguished, while these will not yet have received their full punishment and their fire will not yet be extinguished until they receive their due judgment. Then they will wear out the netherworld: when their judgment is complete, it will wear out and cease, for its continuation is held back only on their account. Concerning this he explains here, from the end of the verse—although “And it shall be” precedes it, it is also repeated afterward to show that it applies to this as well—“And it shall be, from,” and so forth: their judgment then lasts only twelve months from that Day of Judgment following the resurrection. Afterward Gehinnom and all evil will cease from the world, and they too will be rectified, joining “all flesh” that comes “to bow before Me,” in accordance with the interpreters of scriptural allusions mentioned above.
results.heading: Gehinnom’s end and the eventual restoration

results.hebrewQuote: שלמים שהיא אכילה בקדושה זה מורה שתיקנו בשורש פגם הנחש שהיה באכילה, וכמו בלילה ראשונה של פסח שזכו במכת בכורות לפי שעה להתגלות עתיקא, שמכת בכורות היה כנגד כ"ע (כמשנ"ת כ"פ) לכן זכו אז לאכילת פסח שהיא לאכילת קדשים שמורה שהגוף בקדושה, ומשו"ה באהרן כ' וירד מעשות החטאת שמצדו זכה לאכילה בקדושה בחטאת והעולה, ואחר כך השלמים דנאכלים לכ"א שזוכה לכל ישראל גם כן לאכול אכילה בקדושה ובזה ירד בשמחה שכ' בתו"כ, אך מ"מ לא ירדה עוד השכינה לישראל שלזה היה נצרך משה שושבינא דמלכא, וכשנכנס עמו יבקשו רחמים ויברכו את העם שהכניסו הקדושה בכלל ישראל, אחר כך כ' ותצא אש מלפני ה' ותאכל על המזבח את העולה שזה מורה מס"נ, ואחר כך את החלבים שכולל חטאת ושלמים שזכו כל ישראל לתקן הפגם בשורש שיאכלו אכילה בקדושה, ומש"ה כ' וירונו כמש"נ רננו צדיקם בה' ושרתה עליהם רוח הקודש ואמרו שירה ואחר כך ויפלו על פניהם שזה מורה שמשים עצמו כמו שאינו וזוכין להיות מרכבה למדת אין וזה היה לפי שעה ומש"ה נקראו ימי עולם
results.translation: The peace offerings, which involve eating in holiness, indicate that they repaired at its root the serpent’s blemish, which occurred through eating. Similarly, on the first night of Pesach, through the plague of the firstborn they merited for a time a revelation of Atika: the plague of the firstborn corresponded to the supreme crown, as explained many times. They therefore merited eating the Pesach offering, eating sacred food, which indicates that the body is holy. Thus concerning Aharon it says, “He descended after offering the sin offering”: through his own service he merited holy eating in the sin offering and the burnt offering, and afterward the peace offerings, which anyone may eat, through which he enabled all Israel likewise to merit holy eating. With this he descended in joy, as stated in Toras Kohanim. Nevertheless, the Divine Presence had not yet descended to Israel; for that, Moshe, the King’s attendant, was needed. When he entered with Aharon, they prayed for mercy and blessed the people, bringing holiness into all Israel. Then it says, “Fire went forth from before God and consumed upon the altar the burnt offering,” indicating self-surrender, and then “the fats,” encompassing the sin and peace offerings: all Israel merited repairing the blemish at its root so that they could eat in holiness. Therefore it says, “They sang,” as in “Sing, you righteous, to God”: Divine inspiration rested upon them and they sang. Then “they fell upon their faces,” indicating that one regards oneself as nothing and merits becoming a vehicle for the attribute of ayin, nothingness. This was temporary, and therefore these were called “the days of old.”
results.heading: Holy eating, the body, and Divine inspiration

results.reason: The passage directly grounds a Jew’s confidence in the enduring root of his soul and God’s desire for him, rather than his present defects. It is a thematic expansion of the four assurances, not a claim to enumerate those four assurances.
results.hebrewQuote: כשם שצריך אדם להאמין בהש"י כך צריך אח"כ להאמין בעצמו. ר"ל שיש להש"י עסק עמו ושאיננו פועל בטל שבין לילה כו' וכחיתו שדה שלאחר מיתתם נאבדו ואינם. רק צריך להאמין כי נפשו ממקור החיים ית"ש והש"י מתענג ומשתעשע בה כשעושת רצונו. וזה פי' ויאמינו בה' ובמשה עבדו פי' משה ר"ל כלל ס"ר נפשות ישראל בדור ההוא האמינו שהש"י חפץ בהם
results.translation: Just as a person must believe in the blessed God, so afterward he must believe in himself. This means that God has a concern with him, and that he is not a purposeless product that came into being overnight and so forth, like the beasts of the field, which perish and cease after death. Rather, he must believe that his soul comes from the Source of life, blessed be His Name, and that God delights and takes pleasure in it when it does His will. This explains “They believed in God and in Moshe His servant”: Moshe signifies the totality of the six hundred thousand souls of Israel in that generation; they believed that God desired them.
results.heading: Confidence in the soul’s enduring Divine root

results.hebrewQuote: ובבע"ח טהורים מאחר שיצירתם מצד הטוב דאתי ממילא לאדם שלא במתכוין ומסתמא הם נזדמנים לאכילה לאותו אדם עצמו או לבן גילו שיש לו ג"כ אותו כח הטוב. ממילא אותו כח עצמו יוכל להחליץ הנשמה ההיא השקועה באותו כח ברע. והיינו כי כל אכילה מוליד מחשבות זרות והרהורים ג"כ כד"ש (ברכות לב.) מלי כריסיה זני בישי. והוא מצד כח הרע שנתגלגל בו וכאשר הוא מחליץ הטוב הוא מתקנו. וע"ה אסור כי יוכל להיות נשקע ולהיות מוצא מין את מינו וניעור. אבל ת"ח אע"פ שאינו מנוקה בחדרי לבו מ"מ כבר יש לו יתרון על הבהמה מצד חכמתו. ולכן ע"י מחשבתו בד"ת הוא מוציא כח אותה נפש מהתלבשותה בנפש בהמיית וכח בהמה. וכן בפועל הרי מתהפך בשר הבהמה להזין גופו ולהיות נעשה בשר אדם כך בכח מתהפך כח בהמי לכח אדם. וזה טעם מ"ש בזוהר בחכמה אתברירו והת"ח יכול לברר ולתקן נפשות אע"פ שהוא אין מנוקה לגמרי מחותן דברים. רק אם נפשו משוקעת בד"ת ע"י הד"ת הוא מעלה ומתקן כל מיני מחשבות זרות.
results.translation: As for pure animals: since their creation comes from the good that arises spontaneously in a person, without his intending it, presumably they are made available as food for that same person, or for someone akin to him who possesses that same good power. That very power can therefore rescue the soul immersed in the evil form of that power. Every act of eating also generates alien thoughts and imaginings, as it says in Berachos 32a, “Filling his belly is a kind of evil.” This comes from the power of evil reincarnated within it; when he extracts the good, he rectifies it. An unlearned person is forbidden [to eat meat], because he may become immersed in it, like finding its like and being reawakened. But a Torah scholar, although the inner chambers of his heart are not clean, already has an advantage over the animal through his wisdom. Through his thought in words of Torah, he therefore removes that soul’s power from its clothing in an animal soul and animal power. Just as, in physical reality, the animal’s flesh is transformed to nourish his body and become human flesh, so, in its inner power, animal power is transformed into human power. This explains the Zohar’s statement, “Through wisdom they are clarified.” The Torah scholar can clarify and rectify souls even though he is not entirely clean of those things. Provided that his soul is immersed in words of Torah, through words of Torah he elevates and rectifies every kind of alien thought.
results.heading: Torah wisdom clarifies the spiritual vitality in food

results.reason: This distinguishes receptive desire, which can be redirected to holiness, from the aggressive power of anger and domination. It expands the precise male/female symbolic contrast without treating desire itself as intrinsically evil.
results.hebrewQuote: ולפי שיצ"ר דתאוה הוא טוב מאד וכמ"ש במדה"נ (זח"א קלח א) שישאר גם לעתיד רק דאתלבן דלולי כן לא אשתכח חמידו דאורייתא ומצד זה הוא בלתי גבול לכך גם התפשטותו לרע הוא ברבוי. וכל זה רק מצד ומימין שסובבים ומלבישים. ואליך פי' אל פנימיותך ומעמקי שורשך לא יגש דהשורש נשאר ואע"פ שחטא ישראל הוא רק לבוש תוך האדם רע. וע"ז הוא הבקשה חלצני וגו' על העבר מה שכבר נשתקע תוך מחשבות ורצונות אשר לא לה' המה ונעשו ח"ו מלבושים לנשמתו חלצני והוציאני מהם. ועל להבא מאיש חמסים תנצרני פי' אדם שם כללי וחלוקים לזכר ונקיבה איש ואשה. וידוע דהתאוה והחשק נוקבא והכח וגבורה דכורא שממנו נמשכים ברע רציחה וכעס ואביזרה. וזהו איש חמסים שהוא בא לעשוק הנפש שכבר נחלצה ממנה כשרואה שהיא חלושה כטעם איזה גבור הכובש את יצרו וכשאין בו כח לכבוש הוא חומסו אע"פ שכבר בא לטהר ונטהר על העבר כפי כחו הוא משתדל לשוב לעושקו ולחומסו לחלקו בגזילה. וזה כח האיש והוא ע"י הכעס כידוע מהאריז"ל ע"פ טורף נפשו באפו שע"י הכעס הנפש נטרפת ח"ו שהאיש חמסים המכניס הכעס חומסה ואז עי"ז אח"כ יש שליטה לרע בו גם בכל מיני הרהורים וחמדות. וע"ז מבקש שישמרנו להבא מכעס וקנאה ואביזרייהו שלא יהיה נחמס וממילא יהי' שמור ג"כ בתאוה שהיא הנוק' שאין בה כח החמוסה.
results.translation: The inclination of desire is “very good,” as explained in Midrash HaNe’elam, Zohar I 138a: it will remain even in the future, but will be purified, for without it there would be no desire for Torah. From this aspect it is without limit, and therefore its extension toward evil is also exceedingly great. All this is only on the side and to the right, surrounding and clothing the person. “But it shall not approach you” means your inwardness and the depths of your root: the root remains, and even though he has sinned he is Israel, merely clothed within the evil human form. For this we ask, “Rescue me,” concerning the past: extract and bring me out of the thoughts and desires not directed to God in which I have already sunk, which have become, Heaven forbid, garments for my soul. Concerning the future, “Guard me from the man of violence.” Adam is the general term, divided into male and female, man and woman. As is known, desire and longing are the feminine, whereas strength and might are the masculine, from which, on the evil side, flow murder, anger, and their attendant sins. This is the “man of violence,” who comes to seize the soul after it has escaped, when he sees its weakness: “Who is mighty? One who masters his inclination.” When it lacks the strength to master it, he seizes it; although the person has already come to purify himself and has purified his past to the extent of his ability, this power tries to return and rob and seize him for its portion. This is the male power, operating through anger, as is known from the Arizal’s explanation of “He tears his soul in his anger”: through anger, the soul is torn away, Heaven forbid. The “man of violence” introduces anger and seizes it; afterward evil gains power over him in all manner of imaginings and desires. Therefore he asks to be guarded in the future from anger, envy, and their attendant sins, so that he not be seized; consequently he will also be protected regarding desire, the feminine, which does not possess the power to seize.
results.heading: Desire can be purified; aggression seizes the soul

results.translation: The repair for anger is a change of place, as the Torah prescribes exile for a murderer. There was a city of refuge, rather than wandering endlessly, because there is in truth the fear of Yitzchak and holy powers of might that are good, as in “a Torah scholar who becomes heated,” Taanis 4a; this is the city of refuge. In Gilead and Shechem, where murderers were common, they increased the cities of refuge, as stated in Makkos 9b. God does not make impossible demands: since murderers are common there by their innate nature, presumably this quality is also common there in holiness, holy heat, corresponding to the cities of refuge; when it spreads beyond its bounds, it becomes evil murder. Gilead and Shechem both belong to Yosef’s inheritance, for “Do not murder” and “Do not commit adultery” are opposites, as is known. I heard concerning “Your hair,” and so forth, “from Mount Gilead”: hair signifies the judgments and powers of might within a person, and they are holy when they come “from Mount Gilead.” This explains Ahab’s statement, “Do you know that Ramos Gilead is ours?” He knew that there was nothing he could not rectify except the killing of the prophets. Ramos in Gilead is a city of refuge for the murderer: he wished to say that this too had been done in holiness. That is “ours,” but he did not succeed.
results.heading: Gilead: holy severity and Ahab’s failed claim

results.translation: As we find concerning Achiyah HaShiloni’s anointing of Yerovam as king: Achiyah came from Shiloh, from the tribe of Yosef, and concerning Yerovam too it is written, “an Ephrati” (I Kings 11:26), for he was very handsome and guarded against “Do not commit adultery,” which is Yosef’s inheritance. This was not found in Yehudah: concerning Shlomo it says, “He married,” and so forth (I Kings 3:1), while concerning King David it says, “the son of an Ephrati man” (I Samuel 17:12 [the source prints 17:2]). Therefore Achiyah was very pleased to anoint him. Afterward, when Yerovam sinned with the two golden calves, Achiyah prayed to God concerning this error. God then showed him that his love had really been directed only toward Aviyah son of Yerovam, in whom “something good was found,” I Kings 14:13. Therefore, from the time he anointed Yerovam until the statement “The child died according to the word of God,” Achiyah is not called “the prophet” or “HaShiloni,” but simply “Achiyah.” In that statement it says, “According to the word of God through Achiyah HaShiloni the prophet” (I Kings 14:18), for God had rectified this; understand.
results.heading: “Ephrati” and Yosef’s guarded covenant
results.readingNote: The source prints I Samuel 17:2 for בן איש אפרתי; the verse is I Samuel 17:12. The English identifies this explicitly without changing the Hebrew quotation.

results.hebrewQuote: והוא הענין הנזכר בפרשה זו שהיו עסוקים בשקם ותעניתם לאחר מעשה זו שהיה נראה לעיניהם שפגמו במדת יסוד מה שאין לו תיקון וחלילה אפם תקוה. כי גם יוסף בעצמו פגם בהוצאת דבה ולשון הרע ג"כ כפגם הברית שנקרא רע כי ברית הלשון וברית המעור מכוונים כידוע. ולאחר שראה מה שנולד מזה שמכרו אותו למצרים אז התמרמר בנפשו שהוא גרם לזה ע"י שפגם במדת יסוד. ומה גם השבטים בעצמם שבודאי התמרמרו מאד שהמה היו בעלי מעשה שמכרו את יוסף שהיה מרכבה למדת צדיק יסו"ע למצרים והיה נדמה להם שח"ו אפס תקוה. וע"י מעשה זו דייקא היה הקב"ה בורא אורו של משיח והיינו שלימות התיקון של חיי עולם שהוא בחינת משיח בן דוד כמ"ש (סוכה נב.) משיח בן דוד שעתיד להגלות כו' וכיון שראה משיח בן יוסף שנהרג א"ל רבש"ע איני מבקש ממך אלא חיים א"נ חיים עד שלא אמרת כבר התנבא עליך כו' חיים שאל נתת לו. והיינו כי מדת משיח בן יוסף הוא בחינת צדיק להיות נזהר בכל מעשיו בלא שגיאה ומכשול ובאמת אין בזה קיום להכלל ישראל ולכן יהיה נהרג.
results.translation: This is the matter mentioned in this parashah: they were occupied with sackcloth and fasting after this deed, when it appeared to them that they had damaged the attribute of the foundation, for which there is no repair, and, Heaven forbid, that hope was lost. For Yosef himself had also damaged it through bringing an evil report and speaking lashon hara. Lashon hara is likewise like damage to the covenant and is called evil, for the covenant of the tongue and the covenant of the flesh correspond, as is known. After he saw what resulted, that they sold him to Egypt, he became bitter in his soul that he had caused it through damaging the attribute of the foundation. All the more so the tribes themselves must have been exceedingly bitter, since they had actually committed the deed, selling Yosef, who was a vehicle for the attribute of the righteous one, the foundation of the world, to Egypt; it appeared to them, Heaven forbid, that hope was lost. Yet it was precisely through this deed that the Holy One was creating the light of Mashiach: the complete repair of eternal life, the aspect of Mashiach ben David. As stated in Sukkah 52a, Mashiach ben David who is destined to be revealed, and so forth: when he saw that Mashiach ben Yosef had been killed, he said, “Master of the world, I ask You only for life.” [He answered: You ask for] life? “Before you spoke, [David] already prophesied concerning you,” and so forth: “He asked life of You, You gave it to him.” The attribute of Mashiach ben Yosef is that of the righteous person, careful in every deed without error or stumbling; in truth this does not provide lasting existence for the whole of Israel, and therefore he will be killed.
results.heading: Remorse after the sale and the birth of Mashiach’s light

results.translation: The Rabbis did not know the meaning of “Cast your burden upon God.” Rabbah bar bar Chanah said: Once I was traveling with an Arab while carrying a load. He said to me, “Take your burden and put it on my camel.” This means that the sages did not know how far the attribute of trust extends: trusting God to save even in a way the human mind could not expect. In His great love for Israel, God saves every soul with deliverances of which it had despaired. Rabbah bar bar Chanah showed them how to contemplate that Arab, who represents Yishmael, the shell of desire; the camel also alludes to this, as explained in the first volume, parashas Shemini, under “the camel.” He showed them how far the covenant of the forefathers reaches: although Yishmael is unworthy offspring, nevertheless, from the refuse of Avraham’s attribute, some quality of generosity remains in him. Although in his case he uses and extends this attribute outward, contrary to God’s will, nevertheless a quality of generosity remains, until he said, “Take your burden and put it on my camel,” even though Rabbah had not asked him. All this arose because remnants of Avraham’s kindness were found in him. All the more so “God’s kindnesses have not ceased, His mercies have not ended”: they illuminate deliverances that never entered any person’s mind. Even if a soul of Israel is, Heaven forbid, sunk in a particular trait, even desire contrary to God’s will, nevertheless, when it repents, God in His abundant mercy and kindness will clarify it through many clarifications, so that none of Israel shall be banished from Him.
results.heading: Trust beyond one’s expectations and merits

results.reason: The Mei Anthology Behar 1 repeats Dover and is circular. Kedushat Shabbat 3 independently explains how seventh-day blessing appears in the preceding sixth-day manna and why the action receives blessing from the later rest. This is a thematic parallel, not an assertion of the oral teaching’s source.
results.hebrewQuote: וגם ברכת השבת אי' (בב"ר פי"א) ברכו במן שהי' בששי לחם יומים וזו הברכה ביום ו'. אבל אי הברכה בו מצד עצמו רק מצד מה שצ"ז בו הכנה ליו השבת. וברכת השבת הוא מתפשטת ומתגלית ויוצאה לפעל בו. ושבת נקרא מקור הברכות כי כל ברכה בעצמותה הוא בלא שום מעשה כלל. וכמו הברכה דמן שנמצא ביום ו' לחם יומים הם לא לקטו יותר ממה שלקטו בכל יום. ואף נפילת המן מן השמים לא הי' יותר מבכל יום רק שבמדידת הלקיטה מצאו יותר ונמצא בעצמות הברכה לא הי' שום פעולה ומעשה אלא שלענין חלות והשראת הברכה א"א בריקניא.
results.translation: The blessing of Shabbos too is described in Bereishis Rabbah 11: “He blessed it through the manna,” for on the sixth day there was bread for two days, and this blessing occurred on the sixth day. Yet the blessing did not belong to that day on its own account, but because preparation for Shabbos was required on it. The blessing of Shabbos extends, becomes revealed, and is actualized on that day. Shabbos is called the source of blessings, for every blessing, in its essence, comes without any action at all. Thus, in the blessing of the manna, when bread for two days was found on the sixth day, they had not gathered more than on any other day. Even the manna’s falling from Heaven was no greater than on any other day; only when they measured what had been gathered did they find more. Thus, in the blessing itself there had been no action or deed; nevertheless, for blessing to take effect and rest upon something, it cannot do so in an empty place.
results.heading: The seventh day’s blessing appearing on the sixth day

results.hebrewQuote: אמר ליה בר הי הי להלל מאי דכתיב (מלאכי ג',י"ח) ושבתם וראיתם בין צדיק לרשע בין עובד אלהים לאשר לא עבדו היינו צדיק היינו עובד אלהים וכו' אמר ליה עבדו ולא עבדו תרוייהי צדיקי גמורי נינהו ואינו דומה שונה פרקו מאה פעמים לשונה פרקו מאה ואחד. שענין האחד מורה שאף ששונה מאה פעמים עדיין הוא עומד בהתחלה וזה הענין של "ואחד" היינו שעדיין עומד אצלו "ואחד" שהוא אצלו כחדשה בחשק ותשוקה רבה ולא כדברים ישינים וכמו שכתיב (דברים כ"ו,ט"ז) היום הזה ה' אלהיך מצוך לעשות, ודרשו חז"ל שיהיהו ד"ת חדשים עליך.
results.translation: Bar Hei Hei said to Hillel: What is the meaning of the verse (Malachi 3:18), “You shall again distinguish between the righteous and the wicked, between one who serves God and one who does not serve Him”: is not the righteous person the same as one who serves God? And so forth. He answered: both “one who serves Him” and “one who does not serve Him” are completely righteous, but one who reviews his passage a hundred times is not comparable to one who reviews it a hundred and one times. The additional one indicates that, although he has reviewed it a hundred times, he still stands at the beginning. This is the meaning of “and one”: the “one” still stands before him, as something new, with great desire and yearning, rather than as something old. As it is written, “This day God your Lord commands you to perform” (Deuteronomy 26:16), and the Sages expounded that words of Torah should be new to you.
results.heading: The hundred-and-first review: a new beginning

results.hebrewQuote: וע"ז נאמר במדרש (בראשית רבה פרשה ל"ט,א') מי הוא בעל הבירה, הציץ עליו בעל הבירה וכפי הנראה היה לו לכתבו הציץ אליו ולא עליו, אך בראות אברהם אבינו ע"ה את עסק דור הפלגה זאת יקרא בשם בירה דולקת כי היה בעיניו לפלא מאד והרעים בנפשו מי ברא אלה, הציץ עליו בעל הבירה היינו שהשיב לו הקב"ה הלא תראה בעצמך כי לכל העולם לא יקשה ואין אחד מהם שם על לב לאמר מי עשה זאת ואך בעיניך יפלא, ומהרעמות לבך תוכל לשער אשר בוודאי נמצא בורא הסובב כל עלמין וממלא כל עלמין והוא העיר לבך ונפשך לזה, וזה לשון עליו היינו על קושייתו שזה בעצמו הוא תירץ מספיק לפניו.
results.translation: This is why the Midrash, Bereishis Rabbah 39:1, says, “Who is the owner of the palace? The owner of the palace looked out upon him.” Apparently it should have said “toward him,” rather than “upon him.” But when Avraham saw the activity of the generation of the Dispersion, this was called “a palace ablaze”: it was exceedingly astonishing in his eyes, and his soul cried out, “Who created these?” “The owner of the palace looked out upon him” means that the Holy One answered: See for yourself! No one else in the world finds this difficult, and no one takes it to heart to ask who did it; only you are astonished. From your heart’s outcry you can infer that there certainly is a Creator who encompasses all worlds and fills all worlds, and He has awakened your heart and soul to this. This is the word “upon him”: upon his question, which was itself a sufficient answer for him.
results.heading: The question itself reveals the One who awakens it

results.reason: The second oral teaching is independently and explicitly expanded in Machshavot Charutz 10:3: toil precedes insight, yet the insight is recognized afterward as an unearned finding beyond human capacity.
results.hebrewQuote: וכן איתא במגילה ו' ב' לא יגעתי ומצאתי אל תאמן דצריך יגיעה קודמת ומכל מקום נקרא אח"כ מצאתי ומציאה באה בהיסח הדעת (סנהדרין צ"ז ע"א), כי באמת התורה הוא למעלה מהשגת אדם וכל יגיעת אדם והשתדלותו שהוא רק כפי השגתו לא היה כלל להשגה גדולה כזו דדברי תורה שהיא חכמת הש"י, וכשמשיג אח"כ מכיר דהוא מציאה הבא בהיסח הדעת ולא בהשתדלותו בא לזה, אבל מכל מקום צריך ג"כ ההשתדלות בפתיחת חודה של מחט באתערותא דלתתא כי אין השם יתברך מוסר דברי תורה אלא למי שמשתוקק אליהם דעל זה נאמר יהיב חכמתא לחכימין וגו'
results.translation: It is likewise stated in Megillah 6b, “If I did not toil and I found, do not believe it”: toil must precede it. Nevertheless afterward it is called “I found,” and a finding comes when one’s attention is elsewhere, Sanhedrin 97a. For Torah is truly beyond human apprehension, and all a person’s toil and effort, being limited to his own capacity, were not equal to this great apprehension of words of Torah, which are God’s wisdom. When he apprehends them afterward, he recognizes that it is a finding that came when his attention was elsewhere, and that he did not reach it through his effort. Nevertheless, effort is also required, in opening an opening like the eye of a needle through an awakening from below, for God entrusts words of Torah only to one who yearns for them; of this it says, “He gives wisdom to the wise.”
results.heading: Toil first; afterward, the insight is a gift

results.hebrewQuote: ועל ידי שתי הלחם הוא כח ההתהפכות עץ הדעת לעץ החיים, ועל ידי זה הוא המשכת שפע בני, כי אמרו בעבודה זרה ה' א' אלמלא אבותינו שחטאו אנו לא באנו, ומסיק כמי שלא באנו לעולם, היינו דכל הנפשות מישראל שרשם בתורה וכפי התחדשות התורה שבעל פה שבלב חכמי ישראל בכל דור ודור, כך התחדשות הנפשות בכל דור ודור, ואם זכו אבותינו שהיה הכל גלוי בתורה שבכתב לכל ישראל והיו משיגים כולם כל ההתחדשות דדורות העתידות לא היה מקום להתחדשות נפשות, ואף על פה שמכל מקום היה יציאת הנפשות לפועל בעולם מכל מקום הוא כמי שלא באנו, כי כך כבר הכל כלול בפועל גלוי לכל באבות ג"כ ואין שום התחדשות:
results.translation: Through the two loaves comes the power to transform the Tree of Knowledge into the Tree of Life, and through this comes the flow of children. For they said in Avodah Zarah 5a: Had our forefathers not sinned, we would not have come into the world; the conclusion is, “It is as though we had not come into the world.” This means that all the souls of Israel have their root in Torah. In accordance with the renewal of the Oral Torah in the hearts of Israel’s sages in each successive generation, so too is the renewal of souls in each successive generation. Had our forefathers merited that everything be revealed to all Israel in the Written Torah, and that they all apprehend all the innovations of future generations, there would have been no place for the renewal of souls. Although the souls would nevertheless have emerged into actual existence in the world, it would still be as though we had not come, because everything would already have been included in actuality, revealed to all, in the forefathers as well; there would be no innovation at all.
results.heading: Parallel: Machshavot Charutz 15:9 — why later generations bring new souls and new Torah
