results.translation: He then also merits holy inspiration. This is certainly impossible for someone wholly unlearned: he must at least possess a scent of Torah, for holy inspiration leads to the resurrection of the dead, meaning eternal life, and this is possible only through the dew of Torah that revives him. Holy inspiration is the dew of Torah descending from above upon the souls of the children of Israel. As is known, the letters following the letters of the Name Havayah have the numerical value of tal, “dew.” For the Name Havayah is the revelation of words of Torah in actual manifestation: the Torah that Moshe our teacher, peace be upon him, brought down to us and publicly transmitted to the children of Israel. The dew is its reverse side and hidden dimension; it flows continually and is never withheld. Only when there is a vessel prepared and fit to receive that dew of blessing is it absorbed into all his 248 spiritual limbs, which give life to the physical limbs. It becomes so bound to them that it does not separate even after death and the soul’s departure. It remains within the havla de-garmei, the residual breath of the bones, in the luz bone, which never decays or perishes, as our Sages said.
results.heading: Spiritual limbs and the residual breath after death

results.translation: It is taught in the name of our holy master of Lublin, of blessed memory, concerning “To Machir I gave Gilead”: to one who recognizes his Creator I gave Gilead, meaning Eliyahu. His intention follows Pesachim 68a, “Gilead is Eliyahu”: Eliyahu too sanctified ordinary permitted matters, which come from kelipas nogah, and knew nothing of bodily self-enjoyment, the serpent’s counsel, and he still lives. As Vayikra Rabbah 27 states, Eliyahu, who did not sin, already existed: he lives and endures forever. Thus “one who recognizes his Creator” means one who merited the level of daas, as stated in Bamidbar Rabbah, at the beginning of Naso 10: daas means one who recognizes his Creator. “I gave Gilead”: he merits a revelation of Eliyahu, which is also a level of Divine inspiration, called daas, as Rashi explains in Ki Sisa, “and with knowledge”—Divine inspiration. As explained in Netzach Yisrael concerning Eruvin 43a, “Was it not Eliyahu who said them?” and so forth, “Perhaps Yosef the demon said them”: they certainly did not see the speaker, for then they would not have entertained this doubt. Rather, the halachos appeared in the heart of one person in the beis midrash, and they did not know whether this came from holiness, through Eliyahu in the manner of Divine inspiration, or from Yosef the demon.
results.heading: Recognizing one’s Creator and the revelation of Elijah

results.translation: King Shlomo withheld from his eyes nothing they asked for, as he writes of himself in Koheles 2:10, and he followed all the delights of this world. Yet everything was in holiness, with the knowledge that “for all these God will bring you to judgment.” All his pleasures resembled the delight of Shabbos, which is entirely holy, as explained below: therefore he was called “a man of rest,” for all his days resembled Shabbos. This is a taste of the World to Come, where there is neither eating nor the like, but they enjoy the radiance of the Divine Presence: spiritual eating and drinking. So too are the delights of Shabbos and all King Shlomo’s pleasures. This is transforming the bitter into sweet. This was the peace he possessed, with no need for victory through war at all. The woman of promiscuity always seeks to imitate the path of life, like an ape before a human. This was Achashverosh’s feast: eating, drinking, and rejoicing, “when he displayed his wealth,” and “the honor,” and so forth. He too possessed wealth and honor in tranquility, with no need for war. …
results.heading: Holy delight and its counterfeit

results.translation: Afterward God showed Eliyahu the prophet that, after all these things, a person still needs God to agree and place His seal upon them all. This is what is written (I Kings 19:12), “After the fire, a still, small voice.” “Voice” is God’s seal upon “wind,” the will of one who performs good deeds: when they come from God, they are good. “Stillness” is God’s seal upon “earthquake.” “Small” is God’s seal upon “fire.” When God places His seal upon these matters, confirming that the person is not inclining in them toward his own personal interest, they are completely clarified. For even in such matters, when a person yearns for love and fear, he can desire them as he desires the pleasures of this world. Therefore a person needs God to agree that his intention is truly for the sake of Heaven.

results.translation: “I shall remove My hand, and you shall see My back, but My face shall not be seen.” The Gemara, Berachos 7a, says: this teaches that the Holy One showed Moshe the knot of tefillin. Tefillin signify attachment and connection, as in “the bonds of God” (Genesis 30:8). This means that we are bound to the Holy One: whatever may happen to us, we will not separate from Him. In the tefillin of the Master of the world is written, “Who is a great nation,” Berachos 6a: God takes pride in Israel because they bind themselves to Him, and God likewise binds Himself to them; even if they sin, His love will not be severed from them. “But My face shall not be seen” means that God showed Moshe everything that had occurred in the past: he clearly saw what God had been building through that deed. This is “you shall see My back,” the past. “But My face shall not be seen”: the present was not shown to him, because all pronouncements of punishments were given through him.
results.heading: The tefillin knot and the enduring bond behind concealment

results.translation: In truth, Israel too are called “a stiff-necked people,” the opposite of wholeness, but with them the hardness is only in the neck, the person’s back, not in the face, which represents the person’s inwardness: in their faces “all who see them recognize them.” As stated in Eichah Rabbah, “Your face resembles that of the Jews,” and as it is written, “So that His fear may be upon your faces, so that you do not sin.” The Sages, Nedarim 20a, say that this means shame, and that whoever lacks shame of face, it is known that his forefathers did not stand at Sinai. Likewise Yevamos 79a says that Israel possess three traits: they are bashful, and so forth; this corresponds to Yaakov. Shame is visible in the face, as in Bava Metzia 58b, the paling of the face, and it is written, “I am ashamed and humiliated to lift my face to You, for my sins,” and so forth. This is Israel’s quality: when they sin, they are ashamed to lift their faces before God.
results.heading: “Stiff-necked” describes the exterior, not the inward bond

results.translation: “The letters in reverse order” means beginning with the lower heh, which is Malkhut, and it is the Tree of Death (Zohar 155b, cited above). This is the meaning of “and a brightness [nogah] surrounded it”: the kelippah of Nogah; and it is written, “The wicked walk all around,” for “her feet descend to death.” The attribute of Malkhut means that people should recognize the power of His kingship through their own choice. Yet there is also an evil inclination that entices toward evil, and Israel chooses the good and accepts the yoke of His kingship. This is the purpose of the work of heaven. The vine represents Israel, as it says, “You brought a vine out of Egypt,” and, “For the vineyard of the Lord of Hosts is the house of Israel”; and it says, “Why did I hope that it would produce grapes,” etc. The Congregation of Israel is called a vine and wine to allude to repairing the damage.

results.translation: All of a person’s life in this world consists in the effort to reach what has been prepared for him. This includes three things: what serves his own needs and benefit—the purpose of creation being to benefit created beings; what serves the entire creation and benefits all created beings, for together they form one complete stature, and through his actions each person tips himself and the whole world to the side of merit; and what serves the honor of Heaven, as it is written, “The Lord made everything for His sake”—for His praise (Midrash Tehillim 19)—and in Yoma 38a, “Everything the Holy One, blessed be He, created, He created only for His honor.” These are the three names that, according to the Midrash (Midrash Shemuel 23), a person is called. One is the name the Holy One, blessed be He, calls him: the purpose for which he was created to praise the blessed God, who has a particular need for him. Each individual has a distinct role for which he specifically is needed. The name is the root of his vitality, as it says, “Whatever the man called each living creature, that was its name,” as is known. Another is what his father and mother call him, meaning the need that other created beings have for him. The third is what he is called in the book of his generations, meaning the root of his birth for his own sake.
results.heading: Parallel: Machshavot Charutz 19:11 — each soul’s distinct role within the whole

results.hebrewQuote: וגם לפי הפשט על ויעש אברהם משתה גדול ביום הגמל את יצחק שהוא ביום השמיני ללידתו ה"ג מ"ל ג"כ מרמז על שרש תיקון הקלקול הראשון כידוע מאמרם ז"ל שאדם הראשון משוך בערלתו הי' היינו שבעת שנברא עשה האלהים את האדם ישר שהי' מהול רק לאחר הפגם של החטא משך על עצמו את מכסה הערלה. ועי"ז כל תולדותיו נולדים מאתו עם מכסה של הערלה הנמשך מסיבת הפגם הראשון. והגם שגם אברהם אע"ה מל א"ע במצות השי"ת לא הי' בזה עוד שלימות תיקון הפגם להכלל כי רק הוא בעצמו מל א"ע לדעתו. אמנם במילת יצחק אע"ה שהי' הנימול לשמונה תחלה עי"ז נעשה תיקון לכל כלל ישראל הנימולים לשמונה גם בעת שאין לו דעת מעצמו נשרש בו בזה הקדושה שהי' נקרא ועמך כולם צדיקים גם אם יקלקל מעשיו ע"י בחירתו כדאיתא בזוה"ק וגם במשנה קונם שאיני נהנה לערלים וכו' שאין הערלה נקראת אלא על שם העכו"ם וע"ז רמזו חכמז"ל למה קבעו רפואה בשמינית מפני שניתנה מילה בשמיני שצריכה רפואה. והיינו כי שורש המילה בשמיני יורה על תכלית הרפואה והתיקון של פגם הראשון
results.translation: The plain interpretation of “Abraham made a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned” likewise refers to the eighth day after his birth: he-gimmel, whose numerical value is eight, followed by mal, “he circumcised.” This too alludes to repairing the root of the original damage. As our Sages said, Adam stretched out his foreskin. That is, when he was created, “God made the man upright”: he was circumcised; only after the damage caused by the sin did he draw upon himself the covering of the foreskin. Consequently, all his descendants are born with this covering of the foreskin, which follows from the original damage. Although our father Abraham also circumcised himself at God’s command, this did not yet fully repair the damage for the collective, for he circumcised himself alone, with his own conscious understanding. But when our father Isaac was circumcised—the first to be circumcised on the eighth day—this effected a repair for all Israel, who are circumcised on the eighth day. Even before a child has any understanding of his own, this holiness becomes rooted in him, so that he is included in “Your people are all righteous,” even if he later damages his deeds through his free choice, as stated in the holy Zohar. The Mishnah too says, “A vow that I derive no benefit from the uncircumcised,” etc., for the term “uncircumcised” refers only to the nations. Our Sages alluded to this when they asked why the blessing for healing was established as the eighth blessing: because circumcision was given on the eighth day and requires healing. The root of circumcision on the eighth day thus points to the ultimate healing and repair of the original damage.
results.heading: Parallel: Peri Tzadik, Sukkot 44:2 — the eighth day and the root of circumcision

results.translation: For in truth, on a plain reading it is incomprehensible that Joseph the righteous could, Heaven forbid, have been tempted even momentarily to carry out such a deed. Nevertheless, he certainly had a struggle at that time to withstand the trial. This is like the teaching reported in the name of the holy Rabbi Reb Bunim, of blessed memory, on the statement in Sotah 11b: “The midwives feared God and did not do as he spoke to them,” etc.—this teaches that he solicited them for transgression, but they were not solicited. The Sages carefully chose their precise expression, “they were not solicited”: this wording indicates that no feeling of desire for it entered their hearts, such that they could be susceptible to solicitation. Concerning Joseph, however, the wording is “he refused,” meaning that he did in fact feel desire in his heart, but overcame his inclination to withstand the trial.
results.heading: Parallel: Peri Tzadik, Vayeshev 2:1 — the midwives, in the name of Rabbi Reb Bunim

results.hebrewQuote: ועל ידי ההוספה על דברי תורה היינו החומרא דבנות ישראל לישב ז' נקיים גם על יצר רע שבתולדה לעקרו מכל וכל, כי עם ידי קדושת המעשים בתורה שבעל פה בגדרים וסייגים הנוספים על דברי תורה היינו שלא להניח היצר הרע ליקרב כלל כטעם לך אמרינן נזירא וכו' (שבת י"ג.) במשמרת למשמרת שלא יוכל ליקרב בזה מוליד גם בג' ראשונות דמחשבה ורצון שאין נוגע כלל, והם הגורמים זביחת היצר רע לעתיד מכל וכל כמו שנזבח היצרא דע"ז בימי אנשי כנה"ג שהם התחלת התורה שבעל פה כמה שכתוב במקום אחר והם אמרו (אבות פ"א) עשו סייג לתורה ומהם התחלת הגדרים והסייגים, והסוף של תורה שבעל פה שהוא חדושי חכמי ישראל בתורה יהיה בימי בן דוד במהרה בימינו, ויצרא דע"ז הוא ראשית והתחלה דיצר רע ויצרא דעריות הוא הסוף ואז יהיה נעקר הכל על ידי סגול קדושת המחשבה דבור ומעשה בתורה שבעל פה בעולם הזה יהיה כטעם מי מושל בי שגם היצר רע שברא השם יתברך כמה שכתוב (קידושין ל':) בראתי יצר רע הם מושלו לעוקרו מן הלב לגמרי:
results.translation: Through adding to the words of Torah—namely, the stringency accepted by the daughters of Israel to observe seven clean days—one acts also upon the evil inclination present from birth, to uproot it completely. For the holiness of deeds in the Oral Torah, through the boundaries and safeguards added to the words of Torah, means not allowing the evil inclination to approach at all. This is the meaning of “We say to a nazirite,” etc. (Shabbat 13a): a safeguard around a safeguard, so that it cannot approach. This also brings about, within the three highest faculties of thought and will, a state in which it has no contact whatsoever. These safeguards bring about the complete slaughter of the evil inclination in the future, just as the inclination toward idolatry was slaughtered in the days of the Men of the Great Assembly. They were the beginning of the Oral Torah, as explained elsewhere, and they said, “Make a fence around the Torah” (Avot 1); from them came the beginning of these boundaries and safeguards. The completion of the Oral Torah—that is, the Torah innovations of Israel’s sages—will be in the days of the son of David, speedily in our days. The inclination toward idolatry is the beginning of the evil inclination, and the inclination toward forbidden sexual relations is its end. Then everything will be uprooted through acquiring holiness in thought, speech, and deed by means of the Oral Torah in this world. This will be in the sense of “Who rules over Me?”: even the evil inclination that God created, as stated, “I created the evil inclination” (Kiddushin 30b), they rule over, uprooting it entirely from the heart.
results.heading: Parallel: Likkutei Maamarim, Upon Completion of Talmud 3 — the fences of the Oral Torah

results.translation: “Behold, it”—that is, knowledge—“will guide you”: wherever you go, let your actions arise from knowledge. He wished to remove the heart altogether. [When the Holy One, blessed be He, wished to bring him back, as our Sages explain in Sanhedrin 102a on the verse “After this thing,” He took hold of his garment and said to him, “Return.” That is, He took hold of his clothing, for fear is a garment, as is known, and as it says in Avot, chapter six, “It clothes him in fear.” The meaning of this is what the preceding verses describe: his hand withered. Through such an extraordinary sign he received an awakening from above to return. The sign occurred in the withering of the hand, the instrument of action, for that was the locus of his error concerning the definition of particular actions, as explained above.]

results.translation: We find that King David, peace be upon him, said, “Happy is the one You choose,” etc., concerning Aaron (as explained in Bamidbar Rabbah 3). He yearned and longed to offer sacrifices, even though it had already been said, “The outsider who approaches,” etc. [I heard that he merited the fulfillment of his longing by eating the showbread, which he ate to preserve life. Uzziah, who sought to offer incense, was the clarification of David, for the kings from Uzziah onward are the clarifications of the kings from David onward. Each one clarifies the deeds that the earlier one performed unintentionally. Of Jotham, who was the clarification of King Solomon, it says, “Only he did not enter,” etc., because there was no deficiency in him. For all King Solomon’s deeds were holy of holies, and this itself is a deficiency—that he has no deficiency. This is not the place to elaborate.]

results.translation: For the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory, said concerning “naked, but she did not come”: “This matter of nakedness has not yet come.” These are his words. The meaning is that God gave Israel Torah and commandments, which are garments through which they can apprehend His blessed essence. For in this world human ability cannot apprehend His blessed essence except through garments that take on material form; everything we receive comes by means of these garments. At present, when an influence flows from God, He bestows it through the four worlds, by means of the measure of the ten sefirot that the world needs at that time, until it reaches this world, where people can apprehend that influence. results.hebrewQuote: שממית בידים תתפש והיא בהיכלי מלך. שממית מורה על זעף ועצבות מלשון שממה, ובידים תתפש היינו שצמיחת החסרון נמצא אף באנשים גדולים מאד, כי מאן מלכי רבנן, וחכמים ראשי אלפי ישראל ילאו מזה להשלים עצמם שלא ימצא מזה שורש בלבם, וזה היה הענין בעוזיה שנכנס להקטיר קטורת לפני ולפנים לאשר רצה להשלים עצמו בזה, וכל זמן שידע בעצמו שלא נשלם בזה, הבין כי עוד לא נשלם בכל, וקטורת הוא משמח את לב האדם ככתוב (משלי כ"ז,ט') שמן וקטורת ישמח לב, וזהו שנאמר (דברי הימים ב' כ"ו,י"ט) בזעפו עם הכהנים והצרעת זרחה במצחו, לפי שהיה מכיר שאינו נקי בזה, לכן דן עצמו לסכנת נפשות והתיר עצמו להקטיר קטורת לבוא להשלמת נפשו, כי אין לך דבר שעומד בפני פיקוח נפש, והאמנם כי באמת כן עלתה בידו כי אחר זה השיג השלמה שנאמר עליו וצרעת זרחה לשון זריחה, היינו שרק על הגוון היה נראה שעשה מעשה שלא כראוי אבל בעומק השיג השלמה מזה ונאמר עליו (מלכים ב' ט"ו,ה') וישב בבית החפשית, היינו שנעשה חפשי כי היה בשלימות, אך לפי שהיה בין הכהנים ומהם נעלם עומק כוונתו, והיה נראה בעיניהם כמחלל את ה' וכן לפי תפיסתם היה כמצורע, וזה שנאמר ביותם בנו (דברי הימים ב' כ"ז,ב') ויעש הישר בעיני ה' ככל אשר עשה עזיה אביו רק לא בא אל היכל ה', והיא מיעוט ככל אכין ורקין שבתורה שלמדרגה הזאת לא בא, ואלו היה עוזיה מקטיר הקטורת היה בא לחיי עוה"ב מיד.
results.translation: “The lizard can be caught with the hands, yet it is in kings’ palaces.” The lizard [semamit] points to vexation and sadness, from the word shemamah, desolation. “Can be caught with the hands” means that the growth of deficiency is found even among very great people; for “Who are kings? The rabbis.” The sages, the leaders of the thousands of Israel, grow weary trying to perfect themselves so that no root of this remains in their hearts. This was the matter of Uzziah, who entered to offer incense in the innermost sanctuary because he wished thereby to perfect himself. As long as he knew he was not complete in this respect, he understood that he was not yet complete in everything. Incense gladdens a person’s heart, as it is written, “Oil and incense gladden the heart” (Proverbs 27:9). Thus it says, “While he was raging against the priests, the leprosy broke out on his forehead” (II Chronicles 26:19). Because he recognized that he was not free of this, he judged himself to be in mortal danger and permitted himself to offer incense in order to attain the perfection of his soul, for nothing stands in the way of preserving life. In truth, however, he did succeed, for afterward he attained perfection: “leprosy broke out” is expressed by the word zarchah, radiance. That is, only on the surface did it appear that he had acted improperly, while in the depths he attained perfection through it. It says of him, “He lived in the house of freedom” (II Kings 15:5): he became free, because he was complete. But he was among the priests, from whom the depth of his intention was concealed. To their eyes he appeared to profane God, and according to their apprehension he was like a leper. This is what is said concerning his son Jotham: “He did what was right in the eyes of the Lord, according to all that his father Uzziah had done; only he did not enter the Temple of the Lord” (II Chronicles 27:2). “Only” is a restrictive term, like all instances of akh and rak in the Torah: he did not reach that level. Had Uzziah offered the incense, he would immediately have entered the life of the World to Come.
results.heading: Mei HaShiloach I, Proverbs 30:3 — Uzziah’s desire for perfection

results.translation: Israel has no place at all in the world, resembling the blessed God: He is the place of the world, but the world is not His place. Likewise, “The entire world is sustained on account of Chanina, while Chanina is content with,” etc. (Eruvin), for they have no attachment to a particular place, as explained concerning the statement, “Build us a house in the air of the world.” As stated, He gave Jacob the World to Come and Esau this world. results.translation: King David, peace be upon him, was the root of the holiness of the Congregation of Israel, and his enemies were also enemies of God and of Israel; he therefore cut them off through divine inspiration (Arakhin 15b). They were slanderers, and they accused him over the incident of Bathsheba, saying that, Heaven forbid, he was immersed in desire. Although he himself was utterly pure, his heart being emptied [of the evil inclination], because he was king of Israel and the root of all Israel he had to refine his heart so completely that all the hearts of Israel would also be refined. For a king in the world is like the heart in the body, from which the issues of life proceed to all the limbs. That incident therefore came his way, so that through the intensity of his repentance he would awaken thoughts of repentance in all the souls of Israel; when one individual repents, he and the entire world are forgiven. Had that generation merited it, the time of the end would then have come, with the complete slaughter of the inclination. Although their failure to merit this did not arise from him, but from their being slanderers—a trait drawn to them from his enemies, who also included leaders of Israel, such as Doeg and Ahithophel—his complete refinement was nevertheless not revealed. God therefore said to him, “I will not make it known in your lifetime, but only in the lifetime of your son Solomon,” who said, “Remember the kindnesses of David,” and was answered (Shabbat 30a). It was then revealed that David had been attached to the holy kindnesses, the love of the Holy One, blessed be He, and of Israel, rather than to evil loves drawn from the kindnesses of the kelippah, for “it is a disgrace [chesed].” Then his enemies’ faces became black like the bottom of a pot.

results.translation: Just as each food has a particular power to sustain the body, it presumably has such a power within its inner vitality to sustain the soul. The seven species for which the Land of Israel is praised presumably correspond to the seven known attributes of the soul, and dates are the last. I heard that this is why our Sages expounded at the end of Taanit that “an end and a hope” means dates and flax: flax comes from the expression “the cord [tikvat] of thread,” and “an end” refers to the last of the seven species. It appears that dates have the power to instill in the soul a seeking of the ultimate end. The statement in Pesachim that they were exiled to Babylonia so that they would eat dates and engage in Torah means the Oral Torah, which was established in Babylonia. As the Jerusalem Talmud says, honey accustoms the tongue to Torah; therefore the Torah calls it honey rather than dates. And “Malkhut is the mouth; we call it the Oral Torah,” as stated in the Tikkunim. The first chapters of Ketubot and Taanit say that dates loosen the bowels; it appears that they likewise have the power, in the soul, to expel every kind of waste.
results.heading: Parallel: Et HaOchel 13:1 — dates, the final species, and the Oral Torah

results.translation: Our teacher Moses, peace be upon him, corresponded to “I am,” and Rabbi Akiva son of Joseph corresponded to “You shall have no other gods.” As is known, all the souls of Israel are, at their root, each attached to the letters of the Torah. Moses’ soul corresponded to the utterance “I am,” and his work in this world was to clarify His blessed unity in the world. Rabbi Akiva’s soul corresponded to “You shall have no other gods”: to clarify and cleanse every evil, dross, and impurity in Israel’s heart, distancing them from evil, which is included in “You shall have no other gods.” His continual introduction of new boundaries and safeguards meant adding that this too is included in “You shall have no other gods,” and that one must cleanse oneself of it as well. Likewise, all the laws of forbidden and permitted, invalid and valid, impure and pure, serve to distinguish evil from good.
results.heading: Mei HaShiloach I, Bo 5 — Moses, Rabbi Akiva, and the first two commandments

results.translation: The holy Zohar says on the verse “The voice was heard,” etc., that one must pray quietly, with that voice which is not audible, and this is the prayer that is always accepted. Its sign is “the voice was heard”: kol, “voice,” written without a vav, was heard. This requires explanation, for it is written, “Indeed, God has heard; He has attended to the voice of my prayer,” where kol is written with a vav. The intended meaning, however, is not the audible sound heard by human ears, but the cry that emerges from the innermost point of the heart. It cannot be understood within human apprehension, except by the One who knows the heart’s secrets, as we say, “Hear our cry, Knower of secrets.” This is the quiet voice that is accepted, for through it all defects are repaired down to their root. Midrash Tanchuma 5 says, “‘The voice was heard’—this voice is none other than Judah’s voice, as it says, ‘Hear, O Lord, the voice of Judah.’” For “Judah approached him and said, ‘Please, my lord’” was an approach in prayer to God from the depths of the heart (as stated in Bereishit Rabbah and explained in discourses 1 and 2), having no recourse except to await His salvation. Through this, even the root was clarified and repaired, and a preparation was made for the entire collective of Israel.
results.heading: Parallel: Peri Tzadik, Vayigash 14:1 — the inaudible voice from the heart’s depths

results.translation: Scripture uses the expressions “joyful” and “a good heart,” alluding to the Written Torah and the Oral Torah. Concerning the Written Torah, the language of joy applies, as it says, “The precepts of the Lord are upright, gladdening the heart.” The Oral Torah concerns the bettering of the heart, as it is written of Boaz, “His heart was good”—through words of Torah. I heard from my master and teacher, of blessed memory, that this is why the Talmud in many places says, “According to his heart [alibbei]”: the words of the Oral Torah emerge from the walls of a person’s heart, in accordance with the holy feeling within his heart. As it says, “For with abundant wisdom comes abundant vexation”: through abundant wisdom, the Oral Torah, the heart is straightened from its abundant vexation, and the abundant vexation is repaired.

results.translation: That is, our father Yaakov, peace be upon him, thought that through the aspect of “Israel”—meaning through the power of Torah—the clarification would at least thereby be completed, which is what the name “Israel” indicates, as explained above. As stated in Kiddushin 30b, “I created the evil inclination, and I created Torah as its seasoning,” and in the holy Zohar (I,202a), “You have nothing that breaks the evil inclination except Torah.” … The kingship of the house of David was also divided at Shechem. This too is connected with the same matter, for it occurred through Yeravam ben Nevat, who likewise possessed the power of Torah. As Sanhedrin 102a expounds on “alone in the field,” all Torah scholars appeared before them like the grass of the field. On “he was wearing a new garment,” it explains that Yeravam’s Torah had no blemish, like a new garment. We heard from the holy Rebbe, of blessed memory, that this was why Yeravam found favor in the eyes of Achiyah HaShiloni: Yeravam was clean of desires, as his being called “Ephratite” indicates, and Achiyah came from Shiloh, in Yosef’s territory. Indeed, Mashiach ben Yosef will emerge from him, from Aviyah son of Yeravam, as stated in Zohar Chadash, Balak, and as it says of him, “Because in him something good was found.” It was shown to him [Yaakov] that even this is not yet the completion of clarification. As Bereishis Rabbah expounds on “Behold, this master of dreams”: this one is destined to induce them to follow the Baals, meaning through Yeravam’s calves, as explained in Matnos Kehunah. For even through Mashiach ben Yosef the redemption will not be complete; it will come specifically through Mashiach ben David.
results.heading: Pri Tzaddik, Vayeshev 1:1 — Yeravam’s Torah and the completion through David

results.translation: Why do we eat meat and fish on Shabbat? The serpent’s principal corruption lay in desire and jealousy: the root of its enticement was to introduce desire and the sensation of personal enjoyment, as is known. Thus it is written, “The woman saw,” etc., and “that it was desirable,” etc. It also says, “She gave also to her husband with her.” This arose from jealousy, as Rashi explains: so that she would not die while he lived and married another (also Pirkei deRabbi Eliezer 13). Our principal work is to repair its corruption and bring these two aspects exclusively into holiness, as it says, “Let your heart not envy sinners, but only in the fear of the Lord all the day.” That is, one should be jealous concerning fear of God, as it says, “The jealousy of scholars increases wisdom” (Bava Batra 21a). This is the meaning of Behemoth upon a thousand hills—the wild ox—and Leviathan, which are prepared for the righteous in the future, when the evil inclination will be removed. They represent the two inclinations of desire and anger. These are present in these two living creatures, as Berakhot 61a states that an animal too has an evil inclination, for we see it damaging, biting, and kicking: this is the evil inclination toward killing. Leviathan represents desire, for it grows primarily in water, and concerning Leviathan Bava Batra 74b says that castrating the male and cooling the female would not suffice, for fish are promiscuous (as explained in discourse 5 and Toldot, discourse 4). Thus we eat meat and fish on Shabbat in order to repair the serpent’s corruption through holy eating and bring the two aspects into holiness.
results.heading: Parallel: Peri Tzadik, Vaera 11:1 — Leviathan, the wild ox, and the two inclinations

results.translation: On Yom Kippur the latter Tablets were given: the repair that follows damage and departure from the proper order. From there comes the nourishment of the Oral Torah, as is known: “Remember” corresponds to the masculine and “Observe” to the feminine, and the second Tablets belong to the mystery of the feminine. In the future, when the entire Oral Torah is completed, it too will become Written Torah: these are the latter Tablets. The Written Torah corresponds to the first Tablets, which are at present the broken Tablets resting in the Ark. Then, when death is swallowed up forever, the first Tablets too will return to their original state, as stated in the Tikkunim, that death is the mystery of the breaking of the Tablets. Then the light of the moon will be like the light of the sun, corresponding to the Tablets of the Written Torah, and the light of the sun will be like the light of the seven days, by which a person could see from one end of the world to the other. This is the light of the first Tablets, through which there was then freedom from the angel of death and the evil inclination, as there will be in the future, when there will no longer be any partition separating and concealing the light at all.
results.heading: Parallel: Machshavot Charutz 12:9 — the future restoration of the first Tablets

results.hebrewQuote: ואלהי מסכה לא תעשו לכם. מסכה היא דבר הניתך ממתכות שלא יוכל לזוז ולהתנענע וגם באדם ימצא שירגיל את עצמו בהנאת עוה"ז אף בהנאה קטנה עד שלא יוכל לפרוש ממנה זה יקרא מסכה. ועל זה צוה הש"י לנו שלא נאמר שאנו מורגלים בדבר שלא נוכל לפרוש, רק בכל דבר הנאה שיגיע לאדם צריך לסלק את עצמו מכל נגיעותיו, ובאם אחר סילוק והסרת נגיעותיו עוד ישאר לו זה החשק אז ידע בברור כי מאת ה' היא, כמו שמצינו בירמיה הנביא ע"ה (ירמיה מ"ב) ששאלו לו האנשים באם ישובו למצרים והוא התרה בהם אם ישמעו לדבריו והבטיחו לו שלא יסורו מדבריו ימין ושמאל. ואח"כ כאשר אמר להם שלא ישובו אמרו לו ברוך בן נריה מסית אותך (ירמיה מ"ג,ג'). וזה לא היה מפני שחשדו אותו שלא אמר להם מפי הש"י רק מדעתו כי היה מוחזק אצלם לנביא ה', וגם כי דבר כזה לא היה נכתב בדברי תורה. אך חשדו אותו כי מאהבתו לברוך בן נריה רוצה שישארו בא"י, כי רצה שברוך ישיג נבואה וכל התחלת השגות נבואה אינו רק בא"י כידוע, ומחמת אהבתו הוא נוגע לדבר הזה ונדמה לו שגם רצון הש"י נוטה לזה. כי גם בנבואה צריך בירר גדול אם הוא אמתיות מאת הש"י, כמו שמצינו בירמיה עצמו בשעה שהיה חבוש בבית האסורים והיה לו נבואה שיקנה השדה מאת חנמאל בן שלום דודו ואח"כ כאשר בא חנמאל בן שלום דודו ואמר לו שיקנה מאתו השדה אז אמר ואדע כי דבר ה' היא (ירמיה ל"ב,ח'), משמע שעד עתה היה מסופק בדבר אם היא מאת ה' פן היא ביען כי רצונו לקנות השדה, לכן ידמה לו שגם רצון ה' היא לזה, וזה נקרא מסכה היינו עקשות ברצון אחד. לכן צריך האדם לברר את עצמו בכל עניניו ולהסיר מאתו כל נגיעותיו וגם ירמיה בירר את עצמו אח"כ שנאמר ויהי מקץ עשרה ימים השיב להם שלא ישובו ואמר להם אם שוב תשבו בארץ הזאת (ירמיה מ"ב,י'), והיתה לו נבואה שברוך לא ישיג עוד נבואה כמ"ש כה תאמר אליו וכו', ואתה תבקש לך גדולות (ירמיה מ"ה,ה'), ובירר והוכיח צדקו לעינים, כי עוד לא נמצא בו נגיעה לברוך, כי ברוך לא ישיג עוד נבואה, כי כל השפעות נבואה לנביאים אינו רק בשביל ישראל, ובשעה שישראל בגלות אין הנבואה שורה על הנביאים, ואף שנכתב המאמר הזה קודם, אין מוקדם ומאוחר בתורה.
results.translation: “You shall not make molten gods for yourselves.” A molten object is something cast from metal that cannot move or change. A person too may grow so accustomed to a worldly pleasure, even a small pleasure, that he cannot detach himself from it; this is called a molten object. God therefore commanded us not to say that we are so accustomed to something that we cannot detach ourselves. Rather, with every pleasure that comes to a person, he must remove all his personal interests. If, after putting aside and removing those interests, the desire still remains, he will know clearly that it is from God. We find this concerning the prophet Jeremiah (Jeremiah 42). The people asked him whether they should return to Egypt. He warned them to consider whether they would listen to him, and they promised not to depart from his words to the right or left. Yet afterward, when he told them not to return, they said, “Baruch son of Neriah is inciting you” (Jeremiah 43:3). This was not because they suspected that he had spoken from his own mind rather than from God, for they accepted him as a prophet of the Lord; moreover, such a thing would not have been recorded in the words of Torah. Rather, they suspected that, because of his love for Baruch son of Neriah, he wanted them to remain in the Land of Israel, since he wanted Baruch to attain prophecy, and the initial attainment of prophecy occurs only in the Land of Israel, as is known. His love made him personally interested in the matter, and it seemed to him that God’s will also inclined in that direction. Even in prophecy, great clarification is needed to determine whether it truly comes from God. We find this concerning Jeremiah himself: while he was confined in prison, he received a prophecy that he should buy the field from Hanamel son of Shallum, his uncle. Only afterward, when Hanamel came and told him to buy the field, did he say, “Then I knew that it was the word of the Lord” (Jeremiah 32:8). This implies that until then he doubted whether it came from God, lest his own wish to buy the field make it seem to him that this was also God’s will. This is called a molten object: stubborn attachment to a single desire. A person must therefore clarify himself in all his affairs and remove all his personal interests. Jeremiah too afterward clarified himself: “At the end of ten days,” he replied that they should not return, telling them, “If you will remain in this land” (Jeremiah 42:10). He received a prophecy that Baruch would no longer attain prophecy, as it says, “Thus shall you say to him,” etc., “Do you seek great things for yourself?” (Jeremiah 45:5). He clarified and demonstrated his righteousness openly, for he no longer had any personal interest regarding Baruch: Baruch would not attain prophecy. All the prophetic influence received by the prophets is only for Israel’s sake; when Israel is in exile, prophecy does not rest upon the prophets. Although this statement is written earlier, the Torah’s order is not necessarily chronological.
results.heading: Mei HaShiloach I, Kedoshim 6 — Jeremiah, Baruch, and personal interest

results.translation: The omer is of barley, which is animal food, like the sotah’s offering: because she performed an animal act, her offering is animal food (Sotah 15b). She thereby brings her animal soul near to God. Sexual immorality and every corruption of the covenant are animal acts; their repair is through the omer offering, in which a person offers all his animal powers to God as well. Then we begin counting the days toward the giving of the Torah, when people become free from the evil inclination and the angel of death. The term “sin-offering” [chattas] is not written concerning it, for there is no longer any sin at all. His animal activity too is refined during the forty-nine days of the counting, to become sevenfold purified, and the holiness of Yesod, the holy covenant, is refined. Through the holiness of Shavuot he then merits an influence of children: on Atzeret the world is judged concerning the fruit of the tree (Rosh Hashanah, cited above), and “man is a tree of the field,” so he merits an influence of fruit according to his kind.
results.heading: Parallel: Machshavot Charutz 15:2 — the barley offering and the animal powers

results.translation: The robe, which covers the whole body and corresponds to the tunic, concerns the very essence of the power of the Maker within what He has made. It reveals Hashem’s secret within the essential power of the soul, which is a portion of God. This concerns slander, which corresponds to bloodshed, as it says, “Their tongue is a slaughtering arrow,” etc. But David has already cut them off through divine inspiration, as stated in Arachin 15b. One therefore needs the interpreters of scriptural allusions in the chapter Chelek (Sanhedrin 105a), who teach that they too have a portion in the World to Come, and the discussion of King David’s coming: “It is upon Me,” etc.; see there. “Allusions” means the imprint of the soul itself, revealed through the power of the Maker within what He has made. The “interpreters” are those who attain the revelation and splendid garments of Hashem’s secret within it. Through revealing the depths of the Jewish soul’s root, they understand that it cleaves to the living God and has no severance whatsoever at the end of everything, when all the various garments of choice—which are all garments of this world—are gone. From the standpoint of the soul’s own essence, a portion of God above, every individual Jewish soul is completely bound to Hashem. This atones even for the cutting off of the root, Heaven forbid. Through words of Torah a person likewise merits splendid garments, through thought, speech, and action in words of Torah. Therefore “tents” too raise one from every impurity, etc. (Berachos 16a). Regarding slander too the Sages said that its remedy is to occupy oneself with Torah (Arachin, there). Through words of Torah one likewise merits all the High Priest’s garments, garments that atone for his soul from every kind of evil completely, as explained above.
results.heading: Torah Repairs the Soul’s Garments and Reveals Its Unbroken Root

results.hebrewQuote: מכל מקום הרי מלאכי השרת השפיעו לו עושר כזה, שהוא היה לו כח בקדושתו להכניס גם כל המותרות אל הקדושה. דגם מה שנראה מותר בעולם, אף הוא מכלל ברייתו של עולם, ובזה הוא העלאת הנפשות הנראות כמותרות כמו שכתבתי לעיל. ועל כן גם הוא היה דוגמת משיח כמו שאמרו בפרק חלק כגון רבי. ובמדרש איכה אמרו עליו רוח אפינו משיח ה' נלכד בשחיתותינו. היינו דמה שלא עלה בידו היה רק מפני עון הדור ובשחיתותינו ושאין הדור זכאי, אבל הוא היה זכאי ולא מת, וכמו שאמרו בכתובות (ק"ג סוף ע"א) דכל בי שימשי אתי לביתיה. … אבל אצל רבי נתייחס המותרות לאהורייריה ואצלו אף שהיה בגדר מותרות, הוא היה יכול להכניס הכל לקדושה. ובימי ר' פנחס בן יאיר שלא הגיע עדיין לשלימות הקדושה ראה אצלו הפרידות לבנות המזיקות ואמר מלאך המות בביתו כו'. ובודאי לא היה רבי קונה מזיק בביתו, וצריך לומר דהיו קונים הפרידות קטנות, דבזה היה ברכת הצלחה כשיוגדלו ויצליחו, ואז בקטנותן לא היה אפשר להכיר עדיין הא דחיוורן ריש כרעייהו, דאחר כן היו מתלבנות. וז"ש מאלך המות בביתו. ואחר כן אמר לו שאין שום תקנה, אפילו להרגן אין יכול ואם כן אנוס הוא מה יעשה. וצריך לומר דהכוונה אמר לו הזמין השם יתברך תקלה זו לביתו ואין דבר רע יורד מן השמים, ואם השפע מהשם יתברך לא היה נשפע מלאך המות ודבר המזיק. ועל כרחך שיש בקרב לבבו עדיין איזה חמדה למותרות שמזה בא השפעה זו מצד היצר ולא מצד הקדושה.
results.translation: Nevertheless, the ministering angels bestowed such wealth upon him because, through his holiness, he had the power to bring even every surplus into holiness. Even what appears superfluous in the world belongs to the world's creation; this is the elevation of souls that appear superfluous, as I wrote above. Therefore he too resembled the Messiah, as they said in the chapter Chelek: ‘Such as Rabbi.’ In Eichah Rabbah they applied to him, ‘The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of Hashem, was caught in their pits.’ His failure to accomplish it resulted only from the generation's sin—‘in our corruptions’—and its lack of merit; he himself was worthy and did not die, as they said in Kesubos 103a: every Sabbath eve he would come to his home.… With Rabbi, however, the surplus was attributed to his stable keeper; although it was surplus in relation to him, he could bring everything into holiness. In Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair's time, before [Rabbi] had yet reached complete holiness, Rabbi Pinchas saw the harmful white mules in his house and said, ‘The Angel of Death is in his house!’ Certainly Rabbi would not purchase a dangerous creature for his home. We must therefore say that the mules were purchased young, when the blessing of success lay in their growing and thriving. At that age their white lower legs could not yet be recognized; they became white afterward. Hence his statement, ‘The Angel of Death is in his house.’ He subsequently told him that no remedy existed: he could not even kill them. If so, he was constrained—what could he do? Rather, the meaning must be that Hashem had brought this stumbling block into his home. No evil descends from Heaven; had the bounty come from Hashem, an Angel of Death and a harmful thing would not have been bestowed. Necessarily, then, there was still some craving for surplus within the depths of his heart, from which this bounty came through the inclination rather than through holiness.
results.heading: Parallel: Yisrael Kedoshim 5:34

results.translation: This was said concerning the tribe of Asher in accordance with what I heard from the holy Rebbe, of blessed memory. He said that Amos, who belonged to Asher and came from Tekoa, spoke the passage ‘Are you not like the children of the Kushites?’ It is founded upon the cry of young people: one who has damaged the covenant is called unsightly and a Kushite, the opposite of Yosef, who is called ‘beautiful in form and beautiful in appearance.’ This is because that damage occurs more commonly in this tribe. These are the substance of his words. That is, this tribe was given particular power to repair the serpent's damage and corruption. Its root was in eating; afterward it developed into the serpent's coming upon Chavah and imparting contamination to her, from which the corruption of the one hundred and thirty years developed. Since this tribe was given the greatest power to repair the root of the corruption in eating, the damage is more common in it, and it repairs that damage most powerfully. We find the same with Yehudah: the damage involving Er and Onan is mentioned there, yet David, the root of life, emerged from it. As the Zohar says (I,207b), ‘King David is living, and his closeness is to the Life of the worlds.’ From him will emerge Mashiach, whose numerical value equals nachash, ‘serpent’; he will repair all the serpent's damage and corruption, and death will be swallowed up forever. This tribe likewise received particular power to repair the root of the serpent's corruption in eating, as explained. ‘From Asher, his bread is rich’: oil alludes to wisdom, as they say in Menachos 85b, ‘Because the people of Tekoa are accustomed to olive oil, wisdom is common among them.’ The principal repair of this damage comes through wisdom and Torah, as they say in Sukkah 52b: ‘If this repulsive one encounters you, draw him into the study hall.’ The meaning is to draw him into holiness, so that the joy of Torah learning will come from him, as it will in the future. For that purpose he was created, as they say in Kiddushin 30b: ‘I created the evil inclination, and I created Torah as its seasoning’—the inclination of desire, concerning which He said, ‘I created the evil inclination.’

results.translation: ‘Eleven days from Chorev,’ and so forth. Receiving the Torah means that they acquired words of Torah in their minds, intellect and understanding. The Land of Israel alludes to words of Torah becoming firmly established in the body, like a peg that will not move. Moshe Rabbeinu told them: when you received the Torah at Chorev, you imagined it had become established in your hearts and that there was no distance between mind and heart. For it is ‘eleven days from Chorev,’ yet they traveled it in three days, as Rashi explains. In truth, however, there is a great distance from the mind to establishment within the heart. That distance consists of all forty years in the wilderness and all the stumbling blocks they encountered then. Through these their hearts were refined until they were worthy to enter the Land of Israel and to have words of Torah firmly established within them. For a person does not fully understand words of Torah unless he has stumbled in them, as the Gemara says in Gittin 43a. All their distress and endurance served so that afterward words of Torah would be established within them with complete permanence. Concerning this Shlomo HaMelech said (Psalms 127:1), ‘Unless Hashem builds the house … those who eat the bread of sorrows; so He gives His beloved sleep.’ To Hashem's beloved, Hashem imparts words of Torah within his heart even while he sleeps and does not exert himself so greatly. Shlomo said this about himself.

results.translation: After the giving of the Torah, the renewal of halachos was entrusted to the souls of Israel. Therefore Torah scholars are called builders, who engage in building the world, as stated in Shabbos 114a: they build every day through the renewal of words of Torah within their souls, tasting a fresh flavor each day, rather than proceeding from habit. They expounded this from the word “you shall serve”: the essence of service is that desire is renewed in the soul beyond its natural disposition. Thus, concerning the verse “between one who serves God and one who has not served Him,” it says: “One who reviews his chapter one hundred times is not comparable to one who reviews his chapter one hundred and one times,” and so forth; “Go and learn from the donkey drivers’ market,” and so forth, as stated in Chagigah 9b. Sefer HaTanya writes that the customary practice was to review one’s chapter one hundred times; someone who goes one repetition beyond the customary practice is called “one who serves God,” because his desire has been renewed in this. Similarly, in the service of prayer, each and every prayer, every day, contains something new. As stated in the writings of the Arizal, the clarification accomplished by one prayer is unlike that of another in the ascent of the worlds. In proportion to the soul’s daily renewal in Torah and prayer, the flow of blessing in his food is renewed for him each day of the six working days.
results.heading: The hundred-and-first repetition renews desire beyond habit

results.translation: ‘For Hashem had completely closed … and Hashem remembered Sarah.’ The Midrash teaches (Tanchuma, Vayechi 8): ‘I, Hashem, have dried up the moist tree and made the dry tree flourish.’ ‘I have dried up the moist tree’ refers to Avimelech; ‘I have made the dry tree flourish’ refers to Avraham. Of Avraham it is written (Ezekiel 33:24), ‘Avraham was one.’ From his own side, Avraham was not suited to beget, because he cleaved to Hashem with the utmost simplicity. One who cleaves to Hashem completely has within him nothing other than simplicity and unity with true life. Therefore, when the Holy One wished Yitzchak to be born from Avraham, the episode involving Avimelech came first. Avimelech wished to rob Avraham of what was under his authority, and the judgment was measure for measure. The Philistines possess the world's power of might; this is why Shimshon the mighty continually fought them. This power of might was therefore given to Avraham. Once it was given to Avraham, it was without limit: all the nations' powers are bounded within them, whereas upon entering Israel they become unbounded, because Israel cleave to Hashem also at their root, rather than to any limit.

results.translation: The essence of wisdom and knowledge is their being absorbed within the heart. As was said of Doeg (Sanhedrin 106b), his Torah was from the lips outward, rather than in the heart. The Merciful One desires the heart: the teaching must be absorbed within it, so that the heart follows the knowledge and wisdom it contains. This is called being ‘wise of heart,’ as it says, ‘In the heart of every wise-hearted person I have placed wisdom.’ From this they learned in Berachos 55a that He gives wisdom only to the wise. This means one who receives wisdom within his heart; such a person is called wise. Someone whose wisdom is only from the lips outward is called a fool, as it says, ‘In the heart of an understanding person wisdom rests, but in the midst of fools it is made known.’ He does possess wisdom that can be made known, yet Scripture calls him a fool because it is not within his heart, where it would rest. A fool has no desire for understanding, but only for displaying his heart. As the Zohar says concerning Bilaam (Balak 193b), praising himself is a sign that he knows nothing. Certainly the Torah did not record a falsehood when he described himself as ‘knowing the knowledge of the Most High.’ Rather, all his knowledge was from the lips outward. Once he had uttered it, nothing remained within him, and he was dismissed and went away, as explained on ‘Behold, I am going.’ Although he knew the knowledge of the Most High—that He loves Israel and that they endure forever—he nevertheless did not cease advising ways of making them stumble, contrary to Hashem's will. For the wicked are subject to their hearts (Bereishis Rabbah 34); the heart does not follow the truth it recognizes. Instead, wisdom is forcibly drawn after the impure heart.

results.translation: Whoever is clean of sins of desire requires particular vigilance concerning anger and murder, toward which he is susceptible. As is known, ‘You shall not murder’ and ‘You shall not commit adultery’ are two opposites: the right and left within evil. [As I heard concerning Yeravam ben Nevat, his being called ‘Ephratite’ means that he never experienced a seminal emission; ‘his mother's name was Tzeruah’ indicates that his foundation was anger.] All Yosef's offspring guard the covenant, as is known, yet murder is common there, as Makkos 10a says: murderers are common in Gilead; murderers are common in Shechem. Bava Metzia 84a describes Rabbi Yochanan's beauty. As is known, beauty and comeliness everywhere concern guarding the covenant, as explained above in section 96. It then states that he descended from Yosef, and afterward recounts what happened to him with Reish Lakish. [The Sages customarily do this throughout the Gemara: alongside a person's praise and greatness, you also find what appears somewhat contrary to it, for it is Torah and we must learn it. The same occurs in Tanach.] This arose from the ardor of Torah scholars that prevailed within him, so that he would not forgive. His accustomed infliction of punishment, as in the account involving Rav Kahana in Bava Kamma 117a, likewise suits a person of that temperament, as they say at the end of Shabbos 156a: ‘The master too punishes and kills.’ Although the ardor of Torah scholars is good in every respect, as the Zohar says (II,182b), and Taanis 4a similarly says that Torah causes his anger, nevertheless it appears that his anger did not prosper in this case, considering what ultimately resulted.

results.hebrewQuote: לכן בהקבצו יחד שבטי ישראל ובאו אל יעקב שיברכם אמרו כולם שמע ישראל ה' אלהינו ה' אחד כדאיתא בגמ' (פסחים נ"ו.) ומקודם לא סדרו ביניהם מה שיאמרו רק ששרתה עליהם רוח הקודש שכוונו לדבר אחד. ובזה הראה השי"ת ליעקב תעלומות לבו כל ימי חייו, כי תעלומות לב האדם נתראה ביוצאי חלציו שעל ידם נתגלה מחשבותיו, לכן הראה לו הש"י כי אחדות השי"ת יתקרא על שם יעקב אבינו, כדאיתא בזה"ק (ואתחנן רס"ג.) שמע ישראל ישראל סבא. וכששמע יעקב אבינו אחדות השי"ת מפיהם שמח מאוד ואמר ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד, וזה שאיתא בגמ' (תענית ה':) יעקב אבינו לא מת, כי זה היה עיקר החיים שלו שיכיר כל אדם אחדות השי"ת.
results.translation: Therefore, when the tribes of Israel gathered together and came to Yaakov to receive his blessing, they all said, ‘Hear, Israel: Hashem is our God, Hashem is One,’ as the Gemara says in Pesachim 56a. They had not arranged beforehand what to say; rather, the Holy Spirit rested upon them, and they all intended the same thing. Through this Hashem showed Yaakov the secrets of his heart throughout all the days of his life, because the secrets of a person's heart are seen in his offspring: through them his thoughts are revealed. Hashem thus showed him that His unity would be proclaimed in Yaakov's name, as the Zohar says (Vaeschanan 263a), ‘Hear, Israel’—Israel the Elder. When Yaakov heard Hashem's unity from their mouths, he rejoiced greatly and said, ‘Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.’ This is what the Gemara means in Taanis 5b by ‘Yaakov our father did not die’: the essence of his life was that every person should recognize Hashem's unity.

results.translation: Moreover, it is known that the deeds and service of lower beings have no relationship to the essence of the blessed Infinite. They relate only to His holy emanation, which is also His own essence: He emanated light apprehensible to the lower beings when it arose in His will to create beings, reign over them, guide them, and have them recognize the power of His kingship. This required emanating light through measured attributes, according to the measure of those receiving it. All His names, and every apprehension of angels, seraphim, ofanim, prophets and sages, concern only these emanated attributes. The human being is creation's purpose: the principal intention is a physical person in this world of falsehood, filled with every kind of evil and things that obscure and make one forget the Creator. Choice is placed in his hand, including the choice of evil; nevertheless he overcomes every kind of evil and recognizes the Creator of all worlds and the obligation to serve Him. This was the comprehensive intention of creation. Therefore everything took human form, as Koheles Rabbah, chapter 2, says: ‘Great is the power of the prophets, who liken the formed thing to its Former’; ‘upon the throne was a likeness with the appearance of a human.’ This means the human configuration of Atzilus. Since even the emanated attributes are emanated for humanity, so that a person can apprehend His existence, their measure follows the measure of the perceiver's apprehension. Thus even the emanated apprehension that is perceived has a human appearance. The Torah, the pattern of all creation and the measure of His guidance—according to whose bounded, measured ways all creation came about—likewise has human form: the 248 positive commandments and 365 prohibitions correspond to the 248 limbs and 365 sinews. In relation to this emanated apprehension, satisfaction and, God forbid, diminution of power can indeed be spoken of. Apprehension exists only for those who perceive: without perceivers, what need is there for such apprehension? The Infinite's essence is a light infinitely higher and more wondrous than the light of emanation. All emanation consists only of an apprehension perceptible to created beings—that is, to humanity, creation's purpose. Thus, as human apprehension rises, so does the light that is apprehended.

results.hebrewQuote: שפתי צדיק ידעון רצון. היינו ע"ד שאמרו חז"ל (ראש השנה ו'.) כופין אותו עד שיאמר רוצה אני, פי' ע"י דבורו מכניס הרצון ג"כ בלבו. וזהו שפתי צדיק פי' מה שמדבר משפה ולחוץ בעבור שלבו עדיין אינו מבורר, לזה מועיל לו לברר את לבו לרצון בלב שלם, למשל כשצומח כעס בלבו על חבירו והוא יודע ומכיר זה לחסרון אז עצתו קודם לדבר טוב עם חבירו ואף שאין זה בלב שלם רק עי"ז פועל בעצמו מעט מעט עד שמכניס בלבו אהבה במקום שנאה. וזהו ידעון רצון לשון ידע פי' סדר, שע"י דבורו מסדר הרצון עד שמכניס וקובע כן בלב שלם, כמ"ש (תהלים ק"ד,י"ח) שמש ידע מבואו, פי' שיש לה סדר וקביעת בהליכתה מה שאין כן בלבנה פעמים בא בארוכה וכו' כדאיתא בר"ה [כ"ה.] ע"ש.
results.translation: ‘The lips of the righteous know favor.’ This accords with our Sages' teaching (Rosh Hashanah 6a), ‘We compel him until he says, “I am willing.”’ Through his speech he introduces willingness into his heart as well. ‘The lips of the righteous’ means what he says from the lips outward because his heart has not yet been clarified. This helps clarify his heart until he desires it wholeheartedly. For example, when anger toward another arises in his heart and he recognizes it as a deficiency, his counsel is first to speak kindly with the other person. Although he does not yet do so wholeheartedly, he thereby works upon himself little by little, until he brings love into his heart in place of hatred. This is ‘know favor’: yade'un, ‘know,’ denotes ordering. Through speech he orders his will, until he brings it into the heart and establishes it wholeheartedly. Likewise, ‘The sun knows its setting’ means that its movement has order and permanence, unlike the moon, which sometimes comes by a long path, as they say in Rosh Hashanah 25a.
results.heading: Mei HaShiloach I, Proverbs 10:1 — speech educates the heart

results.hebrewQuote: וי"ל דגלות מצרים היה הכנה לתורה שבכתב שהיה אז בגלות במצרים ושם היה בזלעו"ז חכמת מצרים שהיה ע"י כישוף וכמ"ש (מנחות פה.) תבן אתה מכניס לעפריים ופירש"י כך מצרים שהיא מלאה כשפים אתה בא לשם לעסוק בכשפים. וכישוף הוא בזלעו"ז נגד תורה מן השמים שגם הכישוף חכמה מקובלת וע"י כחות הטומאה וע"י גלות מצרים זכו להרכוש גדול שהוא מתן תורה. וגלות בבל ויון היה הכנה לתושבע"פ שהיא קדושת ארץ ישראל וכמו שאמרנו שערכה של ארץ ישראל היא שורש תושבע"פ (ונת' חנוכה מא' כה) ועיקר התפשטות תושבע"פ זכו בבבל כמ"ש (סוכה כ. ונת' שם) וכן חכמת יון שהיא הפלסופיא שהוציאו מלבם היא בזלעו"ז בקליפה נגד קדושת תושבע"פ. וע"ז נרמז יון בחשך שהחשיכה עיניהם של ישראל (כמ"ש בב"ר) ואז דייקא זכו ישראל להתפשטות תושבע"פ ברוב דעות החכמים שאלו ואלו דברי אלהים חיים וזה התחיל אחר יוסי בן יועזר שנהרג בגזירה זו. ואז התחיל ההתפשטות ברוב דעות (כמ"ש תמורה טו:)
results.translation: It may be explained that the Egyptian exile prepared for the Written Torah, which was then exiled in Egypt. Corresponding to it on the opposing side was Egyptian wisdom, practiced through sorcery. As Menachos 85a says, ‘Are you bringing straw to Afrayim?’ Rashi explains: Egypt is full of sorcery, and you come there to practice sorcery! Sorcery stands opposite Torah from Heaven, because sorcery too is a received wisdom, operating through forces of impurity. Through the Egyptian exile they merited the great wealth of the giving of the Torah. The exiles of Babylonia and Greece prepared for the Oral Torah, which is the holiness of the Land of Israel. As we have explained (Chanukah, discourse 25), the Land of Israel's distinctive worth is the root of the Oral Torah. The principal expansion of the Oral Torah was attained in Babylonia, as Sukkah 20a teaches, as explained there. Greek wisdom, philosophy produced from their own minds, likewise stands on the opposing side, within the husk, corresponding to the holiness of the Oral Torah. Thus Greece is alluded to by darkness, because it darkened Israel's eyes, as Bereishis Rabbah says. Precisely then Israel attained the expansion of the Oral Torah through the many opinions of the sages, of which ‘these and those are the words of the living God.’ This began after Yosi ben Yoezer was killed in that persecution; then the expansion through many opinions began, as Temurah 15b teaches.

results.translation: It is known that our Sages placed each matter in the Talmud in its appropriate location, rather than at random. Because the destruction resembles divorce—as it says, ‘If a man sends away his wife,’ and as our Sages said, they were judged with divorce—its place is in Gittin. Yet in truth Scripture says, ‘Where is your mother's bill of divorce?’ Therefore the particular chapter in which these accounts were placed does not discuss bills of divorce and divorce; it is HaNizakin, ‘Damages,’ because the destruction is only damage. As Bava Kamma 60b expounds, the Holy One kindled the fire in Zion and will pay for its damage in accordance with Torah law. Likewise, this statement, ‘Come and see the difference,’ was placed there in the account of the destruction because that is certainly its proper place. Precisely then it was revealed that even the sinners of Israel, who sinned so greatly that they were judged with divorce, did not thereby lose the name Israel, becoming, God forbid, like all other nations. ‘What comes into your mind shall never be … with a strong hand’: against their will they remain Israel, consecrated to His service. This occurs through the holiness of Shabbos, which is fixed and enduring within the hearts of all the souls of Israel.

results.translation: Every office of authority and every distinction possessed by a person of Israel comes not from that person alone, but from the entire Congregation of Israel. As our Sages teach (Chullin 56b; Shemos Rabbah 37) on ‘From him comes the cornerstone, from him the stake’: its priests come from it, its kings and prophets come from it. The whole nation forms one complete stature. Just as the foot needs the head, so the head needs the foot. The distinction of priests, prophets and kings does not arise from themselves, but from Israel, out of whom and from among whom they are chosen. Thus, as stated in Taanis 30b, throughout the time Israel in the wilderness were under rebuke, the Divine Presence did not reveal itself to Moshe. At the destruction it says, ‘Your prophets too found no vision,’ although they had not sinned. As Yirmiyahu told Baruch, ‘What I built I am destroying … and do you seek greatness for yourself?’ Concerning a king it says, ‘From among your brothers you shall appoint’: through their appointing him, taking him from the innermost depths of the heart of all Israel, he arises and becomes king. For the king in the world corresponds to the heart in the body, as Sefer Yetzirah says; he is the heart of the stature of the Congregation of Israel. Therefore they said in Arachin 17a, ‘The leader is according to the generation.’ The Sanhedrin are called ‘the eyes of the congregation’ (Bamidbar Rabbah 15; Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5), and the High Priest is the head of the Congregation of Israel.

results.hebrewQuote: ושלימות האדם הוא שיהי' כלול בשניהם אהבה ויראה כמו שהיו אבות העולם אברהם ויצחק שהם המדות דאהבה ויראה בפירוד כ"א לבדו יצא עדיין פסולת. ואח"כ נולד יעקב שהיא שלימות הצורת אדם שבמרכבה הכלול משניהם והי' מטתו שלימה והוא הי' השלימות שקודם החטא. ודו ומשיח הם השלימות דבע"ת שאחר החטא וגם הם כלולים משניהם רק אצל דוד הי' האהבה גוברת מכח רות שנקראת על שמו כמ"ש (ברכות ז:) שיצא ממנה דוד שריוהו להקב"ה בשירות ותשבחות. וריוי זה בא ע"י תוקף האהבה שמתעורר הלב לשורר ולשבח. ובמשיח נא' והריחו ביראת ה' שיהי' היראה גוברת שעי"ז יזכה לביעור הרע לגמרי מהעולם בזביחת היצר. ומהיראה יבוא לתוקף האהבה בתענוגים שהוא קדושת היום שכולו שבת שבו נא' אז תתענג על ה' שהוא הדביקות הגמור באור העליון הנעלם מכל רעיון. … וזהו נחלת יעקב שכלול מאהבה ויראה יחד יוכל לזכות לזה כי באהבה לבד צריך הגדרה שלא יבוא לאהבת רעות כאברהם שיצא ממנו ישמעאל ולא נקרא זרעו כי הוא כולו בקדושה ומ"מ יצא ממנו לפי שהוא הי' דבוק באהבה לבד ומזה נמשך מציאות פסולת שצריך לגדרו. וכן ביראה לבד יש פסולת יראת רעות שמזה נמשך מרה שחורה וכעס ומזה הפסולת דעשו ברציחה כידוע. וע"כ צריך ג"כ לגדרים וגבול עד פה תבא. משא"כ ליעקב נא' ופרצת וגו' שהוא קו האמצעי שמושך בלא גבול וא"צ לגדרים דאין בו עוד פסולת ע"י יחוד אהבה ויראה ביחד א"א לבוא עוד לשום פסולת:
results.translation: Human perfection is to include both love and awe. The patriarchs Avraham and Yitzchak embodied love and awe separately, each on its own, and an impure offshoot still emerged. Then Yaakov was born, the perfected human form of the Chariot, containing both. His offspring were entirely whole; he embodied the perfection preceding sin. David and the Messiah embody the perfection of penitents after sin, and they too contain both. With David, however, love predominated through the power of Rus, who was named for him, as stated in Berachos 7b: David emerged from her and ‘sated’ the Holy One with songs and praises. This outpouring arises through the intensity of love that awakens the heart to sing and praise. Of the Messiah it says, ‘His delight shall be in the awe of Hashem’: awe will predominate, and through it he will merit the complete removal of evil from the world through the slaughter of the evil inclination. From awe he will come to intense, pleasurable love, the holiness of the day that is entirely Shabbos, of which it says, ‘Then you will delight in Hashem’—complete attachment to the supernal light, concealed beyond every thought.… This is Yaakov's inheritance: because he includes love and awe together, he can attain it. Love alone requires restraint, lest it turn to evil loves, as Yishmael emerged from Avraham. Yishmael is not called his offspring, because Avraham was entirely holy; nevertheless he emerged from him because Avraham cleaved to love alone, which allowed an impure offshoot requiring restraint. Awe alone likewise has its offshoot of evil fears, producing melancholy and anger, and from that comes Esav's murderous impurity. It too therefore needs fences and a boundary: ‘Thus far you shall come.’ To Yaakov, however, it was said, ‘You shall spread forth’: he is the middle line, extending without limit and needing no fences, for it contains no further impurity. Through the unification of love and awe together, no impure offshoot can arise.

results.hebrewQuote: בס' יצירה המליך אות ו' בהרהור כו' ואייר בשנה וכוליא ימנית בנפש כו' אמר לשון המליך וכ"כ בכל החדשים. והיינו דאות ו' דהוא אות אמת המליך בהרהור, דהרהור הוא מג' דברים שאין אדם ניצול בכל יום (כמ"ש ב"ב קסד:) והיינו דאף מי שנזהר בהם מ"מ לפעמים נכנס בו הרהור בלבו בלא דעת וכמ"ש התוס' (חולין לז:) דמה"ט חשיב לי' לרבותא ביחזקאל שלא הרהרתי ביום וכו' אף שהיא דבר אסור אך מפני הוא מג"ד שאין אדם ניצול כו'. וכן הפי' עיון תפלה שלפעמים נופל הרהור ומחשבה אף בתפלה וכמו שהביאו התוס' (ב"ב שם) מירוש' אף האמוראים. והעצה לה המליך אות ו' שהוא אות אמת ועל ידי זה יוכל להנצל מהרהור.
results.translation: Sefer Yetzirah says, ‘He made the letter vav reign over thought … Iyar in the year, and the right kidney in the person.’ It uses the expression ‘made reign,’ as it does with all the months. The letter vav, which is the letter of truth, was made to reign over thought. Thought is one of the three things from which a person is not spared daily, as Bava Basra 164b says. Even someone who takes care concerning these matters sometimes has an unbidden thought enter his heart. As Tosafos explains in Chullin 37b, this is why ‘I did not entertain thoughts by day’ is counted among Yechezkel's exceptional qualities. Although it is forbidden, it is one of those three things from which a person is not spared. The meaning of ‘examination of prayer’ is likewise that a thought sometimes intrudes even during prayer, as Tosafos cites from the Yerushalmi concerning even the Amoraim. Its remedy is ‘He made the letter vav reign’: it is the letter of truth, and through it a person can be saved from such thoughts.

results.reason: Exact Rav Tzadok explanation of dreams following the mouth specifically through Torah's power to clarify actual deeds and reveal truth. Substantive independent development of the final Mishlei marker.
results.hebrewQuote: רק מי שהאיר הש"י עיניו בד"ת דכתיב בה ‏אמת כמשז"ל (ע"ז ד:) על ידה יכול לבוא על האמת כמ"ש (פסחים שם) ואנן פי' ת"ח היכי התם כי ‏היכי דאיתו אנן הכא כו' שהתורה מאירה בזה לאדם לעמוד על האמת. … וע"ז אז"ל (שם נה:) החלומות הולכים אחר הפה ‏היינו בד"ת שע"י ד"ת יכול לברר כל מעשים שעשה יהי' לטוב ואע"פ שהיו איך שהיו ע"י הפה הוא ‏נעשה טוב שהש"י מאיר עיניו בזה ואז נקבע החלום לאמת כנ"ל דתורה היא אמת ומי שדבוק ‏בתורה הרי דבוק בחיי עולם האמיתים ממילא כל המעשים שלו ע"כ כן כי במקום שהוא האדם שם ‏הוא כולו:‏
results.translation: Only one whose eyes Hashem has illuminated through words of Torah—which is called truth, as our Sages teach in Avodah Zarah 4b—can thereby arrive at the truth. As Pesachim 50a asks, ‘And we’—meaning Torah scholars—‘how are we there?’ ‘Just as we are here.’ The Torah illuminates a person in this matter, enabling him to stand upon the truth.… Concerning this our Sages said in Berachos 55b, ‘Dreams follow the mouth.’ This means words of Torah: through words of Torah a person can clarify all the deeds he performed so that they will be for good. However those deeds may have been, through the mouth the matter becomes good, because Hashem illuminates his eyes concerning it. The dream then becomes established as truth, as explained above, because Torah is truth. One who cleaves to Torah therefore cleaves to true, eternal life, and consequently all his deeds must accord with it, for wherever a person is, there he is entirely.
